The superseded General Schedule, Medicine and Surgery and Foreign Service rates kept governing pay until that agency-specific day, so neither 1975-10-01 nor the signing date 1975-10-06 can be asserted as the single exact first end; this order's own start (Sec. 6) has the same form. state_at_cutoff, first_end and whole_order_end are therefore left open; a reviewer must decide which date convention the project uses for pay-period-dated supersessions.

EO 11883 sec. 5 supersedes 'Executive Order No. 11811 of October 2* 1974' (OCR for Oct. 7, 1974) and sec. 1 replaces the same three statutory pay systems; the end is not dated here because the replacement schedules take effect on an agency-specific pay-period date (see gaps). unresolved_material_gaps: Earlier actual cessation not ruled out: EO 11051 sec. 604 revokes EO 9981 only 'To the extent that the following have not heretofore been made or become inapplicable', which itself contemplates that the order may already have become inapplicable. Whether the President's Committee (paras. 2-6) ceased before 1962 (for example after delivering its final report and being discharged by the President, which historical accounts place in 1950) is not established in the held sources; para. 6 provides that the Committee continues 'until such time as the President shall terminate its existence by Executive order', so the legal effect of any non-EO discharge must be decided.

Para. 1 (the President's policy of equality of treatment and opportunity, to be put into effect 'as rapidly as possible') may have been carried out, restated or overtaken before 1962; its first end is not established.

research_rationale: EO 11667 (April 19, 1972; 37 FR 7763) was read in the held official Federal Register scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 7-8: heading, preamble, sections 1-3, signature block and FR Doc. 72-6171 filing line, so the text is complete). Its operative content is the establishment and composition of the President's Advisory Committee on the Environmental Merit Awards Program (sec. 1(a)), three committee functions (sec. 1(b)), the no-compensation/travel-expense rule (sec. 2) and EPA administrative support (sec. 3); the preamble is narrative. The order has no expiry, sunset, report deadline or condition. Because the committee existed before the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect (January 5, 1973), it would have terminated on January 5, 1975 unless renewed; EO 11827 section 1(8) (held, 40 FR 1218) renewed it until January 5, 1977. Before that date EO 11948 (held, 41 FR 55706) section 4(a)(1) revoked EO 11667, and section 5 makes EO 11948 effective December 31, 1976; section 3's separate January 16, 1977 date applies only to EO 11868. So the first and only end of every clause is the revocation effective December 31, 1976, and the whole-order end is that date. The OFR catalog (revoked by EO 11948; continued by EO 11827) and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (continued by EO 11827; revoked by EO 11948) agree, and no other amendment, revocation or statute affecting the order was found in the bounded searches listed (no U.S. Code or eCFR citation of the order). Quotations are the scan's OCR text, kept as printed (soft hyphens at line ends).

research_rationale: EO 11864 (June 13, 1975; 40 FR 25579) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 11, complete from heading to FR Doc. 75-15839 and footnote). It is a single amending sentence: effective June 1, 1975, section 1 of EO 11861 (placing positions in level IV of the Executive Schedule) is revised at paragraph (13) to read 'Adviser to the Secretary (Counselor, Economic Policy Board), Department of the Treasury, to terminate effective August 1, 1975' (the OCR renders the closing '1975.”' with its footnote mark as '1,197571'; EO 11877 section 1(b), held, quotes the same paragraph with the date as 'August 1, 1975'). The order therefore fixed its own end: the placement lapsed on August 1, 1975, and that is the first end of the only clause and the whole-order end. The formal supersession came a month later: EO 11877 (September 2, 1975; 40 FR 40797, held), which states no effective date, superseded EO 11864 (section 2) and replaced paragraph (13) with an open-ended placement (section 1(b)); it is recorded as a later event, not as the first end, following the rule that a formal supersession can follow an earlier cessation under the order's own terms. A current-law note at 5 U.S.C. 5317 and the OFR catalog describe the same history (the note says the paragraph was 'to terminate effective August 1, 1975' and was superseded by EO 11877); the 1989 OFR Codification table lists EO 11864 as amending EO 11861 and superseded by EO 11877. The machine current-law hits for this order are that historical note, not a continuing basis.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12148 revokes EO 10529 outright. Its only transition rule, section 2-302, lets the FEMA Director continue to perform functions transferred to him by section 1 of EO 12148 notwithstanding the revocations; that is a continuation of FEMA's own transferred functions, not a saving of EO 10529's terms, and EO 12148 does not re-enact the 40-hour limit or the other conditions of EO 10529. EO 10529 authorized time-limited training assignments while employees stayed in Federal pay status; it created no vested rights, and pay or travel already allowed for past assignments were completed. No surviving effect traceable to EO 10529 was found.

source.quote:
2- 302. Notwithstanding the revocations, revisions, codifications, and amend­
ments made by this Order, the Director may continue to perform the functions 
transferred to him by Section 1 of this Order, except where they may 
otherwise be inconsistent with the provisions of this Order.

research_rationale: EO 10529 (April 22, 1954; 19 FR 2397) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 1-3: heading, enacting clause, sections 1-5, Eisenhower signature and FR Doc. 54-3141). Section 2 begins on page 2397 and continues on page 2399 after the issue's contents pages; the clause is quoted from page 2399. Operative clauses: the Administrator's recommendation of volunteer Federal personnel for State and local pre-emergency civil-defense training (sec. 1); the agency head's year-to-year authorization (sec. 2) and its three conditions (sec. 2(a)-(c)); continued pay, status and travel (sec. 3); a construction rule (sec. 4); and two definitions (sec. 5). There is no expiry, condition or report duty. Later events, read in the held texts: EO 10773 (July 1, 1958), EO 10782 (effective August 26, 1958, renaming the office in EO 10773's substituted references) and EO 11051 section 603(d) (September 27, 1962) only substituted the responsible officials (ODCM/OCDM Director, then OEP Director or Secretary of Defense); they are amendments, not ends. Section 1's reference to section 3 of EO 10346 describes the arrangements the recommendations serve; EO 10346 was revoked by EO 11490 in 1969, but section 1 does not make its own authority depend on EO 10346, and EO 10529 was still being maintained by amendment, so that revocation is not treated as an end. EO 12148 (signed July 20, 1979; 44 FR 43239, held) section 5-104 revokes EO 10529, as amended, and section 6 makes the order effective July 15, 1979; that stated effective date is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end. The OFR catalog and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (amended by EOs 10773, 11051; revoked by EO 12148) agree. The current-law machine hits for this order are U.S. Code editorial notes recording its amendments and its revocation by EO 12148, not a continuing basis. No other amendment, revocation or statute affecting EO 10529 was found in the bounded searches listed.

research_rationale: EO 12489 (September 28, 1984; 49 FR 38927) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF pages 9-10, complete from heading to FR Doc. 84-26328). The draft's clause list came from a mirror transcription; the inventory here was rebuilt from the official scan: the section 1 continuance term ('continued until September 30, 1985, unless terminated at a prior date by appropriate Executive order'), the eleven committee continuances (a)-(k), the section 2 continuance of the International Private Enterprise Task Force until December 31, 1984, and the section 3 delegation of the President's FACA functions to agency heads. Ends: section 2 expired by its own terms on December 31, 1984; no later continuance of the Task Force exists in the saved catalog (EO 12395 is noted only as continued by EOs 12399 and 12489 and revoked by EO 12534), and EO 12534 section 3(c) revoked EO 12395 as an order whose committee had terminated. None of the eleven section 1 committees was terminated before September 30, 1985: EO 12534 section 1 (held) continues all eleven again, and the catalog shows no intervening revocation. EO 12534 (September 30, 1985; 50 FR 40319, held) section 4 supersedes EO 12489 and section 5 makes it effective September 30, 1985, which is also the last day of EO 12489's own continuance term; that date is the first end of section 1, its items and section 3, and the whole-order end. The OFR catalog (superseded by EO 12534) and the 1989 OFR Codification disposition table (superseded by EO 12534) agree; no U.S. Code or eCFR citation of EO 12489 was found.

unresolved_material_gaps: first_end of every clause left open: the Committee was established on September 30, 1974, after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect, so under FACA section 14 it terminated two years after establishment (about September 30, 1976) unless renewed before then. EO 11827 section 2 (held), which continued the post-1973 presidential committees expiring before January 5, 1977, does not list it, and no renewal has been found; section 5 of the order gave the Treasury the Committee's FACA functions, so a Treasury charter renewal is possible and has not been searched. If not renewed, the Committee ended on or about September 30, 1976 and the EO 11948 revocation effective December 31, 1976 was a cleanup. Needed: Treasury FACA charter renewal or termination notice for the President's Labor-Management Committee (Federal Register, September-December 1976), and the exact FACA two-year computation.

The machine conflict NO_ORDER_CITED_IN_CURRENT_LAW is resolved: 16 CFR part 1027, 45 CFR part 1179 and 5 CFR part 1215 cite 'E.O. 11809 (redesignated E.O. 12107)' as authority for salary-offset rules under 5 U.S.C. 5514, which is evidently a misprint for EO 11609 (the 5 U.S.C. 5514 delegation order redesignated by EO 12107); it is not a continuing basis for this Labor-Management Committee order.

research_rationale: EO 11809 (September 30, 1974; 39 FR 35565) was read in the held official FR scan (fr-originals OCR of PDF page 15, heading to FR Doc. 74-23127). Its five operative sections establish the President's Labor-Management Committee (eight labor, eight management members and a neutral coordinator), state its study-and-advice functions, direct it to encourage sector labor-management committees, direct agency cooperation and assign FACA functions to the Treasury. EO 11948 (held) section 4(a)(2) revokes it, effective December 31, 1976 under section 5. Because the Committee was created after January 5, 1973 and is absent from EO 11827's list of continued post-1973 committees, it may have terminated under the FACA two-year rule about three months before the formal revocation; the first ends are therefore left open rather than taken from the revocation. The OFR catalog (revoked by EO 11948; see EO 11849) and the 1989 OFR Codification table (revoked by EO 11948) agree on the formal history.

1-102. Pay and Allowances for Members of the Uniformed Services. Pursuant to 
the provisions of Section 1009 of Title 37 of the United States Code, the rates  
of monthly basic pay (37 U.S.C. 203(a) and (c)), the rates of basic allowances  
for subsistence (37 U.S.C. 402), and the rates of basic allowances for quarters  
(37 U.S.C. 403(a)) are adjusted, as set forth at Schedule 4 attached hereto and  
made a part hereof, for members of the uniformed services.

Act (Public Law 94-82, 89 j>tat. 419) provides for adjustments in the rates of

U.S.C. 68(a)), at Schedule 7.

allowances for subsistence and quarters for members of the uniformed ser­
vices shall be effective on October 1, 1978. All other adjustments of salary or

research_rationale: EO 11992 (May 24, 1977; 42 FR 27195-27196, held official FR scan text) established the Committee on Selection of Federal Judicial Officers, an advisory committee under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. All fourteen operative clauses (Secs. 1-8, subsections separated) are quoted verbatim from the held OCR text. The order set its own end in Sec. 8 (termination on December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended); that end did not occur because EO 12110 (sec. 1-101(i), effective December 31, 1978) continued the Committee until December 31, 1980, and EO 12258 (sec. 1-101(g), effective December 31, 1980) continued it until December 31, 1982, so the chain is unbroken. Before that extended term ran out, EO 12305 of May 5, 1981 (46 FR 25421, item (b)) revoked EO 11992 and terminated the Committee; EO 12305 states no other effective date, so every clause's first end is May 5, 1981, which is also the whole-order end. No amendment of EO 11992 was found (OFR 1989 disposition table: 'Continued by EOs 12110, 12258; Revoked by EO 12305'; USC note at 28 U.S.C. pt. I agrees). The revocation leaves no savings or residual effect.

research_rationale: EO 12059 (May 11, 1978; 43 FR 20949-20951, held official FR scan text) re-established the United States Circuit Judge Nominating Commission (thirteen panels). Eighteen operative clauses are quoted verbatim; Sec. 6(b) is quoted in two segments because the page break inserts FR page furniture. Sec. 3(b) was rewritten by EO 12097 sec. 1-301 (November 8, 1978), a partial amendment recorded as a later event. The order's own end (Sec. 8: December 31, 1978 unless extended) was overtaken by EO 12110 sec. 1-101(j) (effective December 31, 1978; continued to December 31, 1980) and EO 12258 sec. 1-101(i) (effective December 31, 1980; continued to December 31, 1982). EO 12305 of May 5, 1981, item (a), revoked 'Executive Order No. 12059 ... as amended' and terminated the Commission, with no other effective date, so every continuing clause ends on May 5, 1981, the whole-order end. Sec. 9 (revocation of EO 11972 and EO 11993) operated once on issuance and is recorded as spent on May 11, 1978; its formal end with the order on May 5, 1981 is a later event, and that revocation did not revive the earlier orders. The clause-drafts identity quarantine (the body cites its own number) is resolved: the held page shows the heading 'Executive Order 12059 - May 11,1978' on 43 FR 20949. USC note at 28 U.S.C. 44 and the OFR 1989 table agree (revoked by EO 12305). No savings provision exists.

Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 were amended item by item by EO 11715 (April 24, 1973), EO 11727 Sec. 4 (deleting items (6) and (7), effective as of July 1, 1973 under its Sec. 6) and EO 11736 (August 6, 1973); these are partial amendments recorded as later events, not ends of the clauses, which continued as amended. EO 11768 of February 20, 1974, Sec. 4, superseded 'Executive Order No. 11708 of March 23, 1973, as amended'; it states no effective date, so Sec. 1 and Sec. 2 first end on February 20, 1974, the whole-order end. Sec. 3 operated once on issuance and is recorded as spent on March 23, 1973. The draft's QUARANTINED_RELATIONSHIP_CONFLICT (Stage 19 causal queue) is resolved: its four live leads are exactly the EO 11715, 11727 and 11736 amendments and the EO 11768 supersession read here, and its ten quarantined leads (EOs 11389, 11393, 11409, 11441, 11581, 11587, 11604, 11634, 11676, 11699, flagged PREDECESSOR_NOT_EARLIER_THAN_ACTOR) are orders issued before EO 11708 (most of them amendments of EO 11248), which cannot act on a later order; none ends EO 11708 earlier. The 21 U.S.C. 801 note hit is the printed text of EO 11727. OFR 1989 table: 'Amended by EOs 11715, 11727, 11736. Superseded by EO 11768'.

EO 11983 of May 4, 1977 (42 FR 23127) deleted that item from EO 11861 (Sec. 1(b)) and revoked EO 11872 (Sec. 2); it states no effective date, so the clause first ends on May 4, 1977, the whole-order end. The deletion in EO 11983 Sec. 1(b) names item (14) in its original wording, so the item was still in place until then. OFR 1989 table: 'Amended EO 11861. Revoked by EO 11983'; the USC note at 5 U.S.C. 5317 lists it only among the amendments of EO 11861. No savings provision.

research_rationale: EO 9206 (July 27, 1942; 7 FR 5851-5853, held official FR scan text) prescribed the regulations for enlisted men's quarters and subsistence allowances under section 10 of the Act of June 16, 1942. The text runs over three pages interrupted by the FR contents listing; nine operative clauses are quoted verbatim (Table I with its rate block, which the OCR separates from the labels, its two notes, Table II, its four notes, the advance-payment rule, the department heads' rule-making authority, the dependants' quarters allowance, the dependant definition, and the supersession of EO 8688 and EO 8704 as amended, effective as of June 1, 1942). EO 9295 (effective as of January 1, 1943) amended paragraph C of Table I, a partial amendment recorded as a later event. EO 9386 of October 15, 1943 superseded 'Executive Order No. 9206 of July 27, 1942, as amended by Executive Order No. 9295' and is 'effective as of November 1, 1943'; that is the first end of every continuing clause and the whole-order end. The order has no expiry or condition of its own that ended it earlier, and no later order in the corpus amends or ends it before November 1943. The supersession clause operated once on issuance (recorded as spent on July 27, 1942, the signing date, since a first end cannot precede signing although its effect ran from June 1, 1942). The OFR 1989 table agrees ('Amended by EO 9295. Superseded by EO 9386').

research_rationale: EO 10880 (June 7, 1960; 25 FR 5131, held official FR scan text) allowed indefinite and temporary employees meeting stated service conditions to have their appointments converted to career or career-conditional appointments. Six operative clauses are quoted verbatim (Sec. 1(a) with its conditions (i)-(v), Sec. 1(b) postal substitutes, Sec. 2 definitions, Sec. 3 returning service members, Sec. 4 exclusions, Sec. 5 rule-making). The order's own terms close the agency-recommendation window for Sec. 1(a) one year after its date, but set no date by which conversions had to be completed (Sec. 1(b) conversions wait for career substitute vacancies), and Sec. 3 stays open for any qualifying service member re-employed after discharge; no earlier cessation can therefore be proved from the order itself, and the recommendation deadline is not treated as an end. EO 12107 (effective January 1, 1979) redesignated the Civil Service Commission as the Office of Personnel Management in this order, confirming it was still treated as in force. EO 12608 of September 9, 1987, Sec. 1, revoked it (no separate effective date), which is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end; the same section preserves 'benefits already conferred'. USC note at 5 U.S.C. 3301 and the OFR 1989 table agree.

research_rationale: EO 12295 (February 24, 1981; 46 FR 14113, held official FR scan text) has one operative sentence: under section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 the President, having made the statutory determination and notified Congress, extends the period for continued peaceful nuclear cooperation with EURATOM (already extended by EO 12193) 'to March 10, 1982'. That fixed end date is the order's own term, not a reporting deadline: when it arrived the extension the order granted was used up. EO 12351 of March 9, 1982 gave a new, separate extension to March 10, 1983 (recorded as a later event; it does not amend EO 12295), and the series continued by annual orders. The 1987 revocation by EO 12608 Sec. 1 therefore follows an earlier actual cessation and is recorded as a later formal event. First end of the clause and whole-order end: March 10, 1982, by expiry under the order's own terms. The USC note at 42 U.S.C. 2155 ('extended the period ... to Mar. 10, 1982') and the OFR 1989 table ('Revoked by EO 12608') are consistent with this.

research_rationale: EO 11414 (June 11, 1968; 33 FR 8645-8647, held official FR scan text) adjusted the monthly basic pay of the uniformed services under section 8 of Public Law 90-207, 'effective on July 1, 1968'. Its operative content is one adjusting sentence with four rate tables and three footnote rules (service-chief special rate, the O-1 to O-3 scope rule, senior enlisted adviser special rate); the sentence and footnotes are quoted verbatim, the table figures are cited by page because the OCR scatters them. The order had no expiry, but its rates were the ones next adjusted: EO 11475 adjusted the same rates for every grade, with new footnote rates, 'effective on July 1, 1969'. From that date the 1968 rates no longer governed pay, so every clause first ends on July 1, 1969 (implied supersession by the later adjustment), the whole-order end. EO 11812 Sec. 5(1) later superseded EO 11414 expressly, effective October 1, 1974 (Sec. 6); that cleanup supersession is recorded as a later event, not as the first end. The OFR 1989 table ('Superseded by EO 11812') and the 37 U.S.C. 203 note list it among the pre-1974 pay orders.

research_rationale: EO 11692 (December 15, 1972; 37 FR 27609-27611, held official FR scan text) adjusted the uniformed services' monthly basic pay: one adjusting section, four rate tables and four footnote rules (service-chief rate, O-1 to O-3 scope rule, level V limitation note, senior enlisted adviser rate), quoted verbatim (table figures cited by page; footnote 2 is quoted only as far as the OCR line runs before the page footer). As issued it took effect January 1, 1973 (Sec. 2). EO 11740 adjusted the same rates for every grade with new footnotes, Sec. 2 'This order shall take effect October 1, 1973'; from that date the 1972 rates no longer governed pay, so every clause first ends on October 1, 1973, the whole-order end. EO 11778 (April 12, 1974) afterwards moved Sec. 2's effective date back to October 1, 1972, a retroactive amendment of the period the rates governed, recorded as a later event; it does not extend them past September 30, 1973. EO 11812 Sec. 5(6) superseded 'Executive Order No. 11692 ..., as amended', effective October 1, 1974 (cleanup, later event). OFR 1989 table: 'Amended by EO 11778. Superseded by EO 11812'.

research_rationale: PARTIAL. EO 11525 (April 15, 1970, effective January 1, 1970 under Sec. 3; 35 FR 6251-6253, held official FR scan text) adjusted the uniformed services' monthly basic pay (Sec. 1 with tables and three footnote rules) and set rules for the retroactive payments (Sec. 2(a) excludes increases in lump-sum and similar payments for persons who became entitled between December 31, 1969 and the Salary Act's enactment; Sec. 2(b) gives the Secretary of Defense authority to prescribe other retroactive-pay rules). All six clauses are quoted verbatim. The Sec. 2 rules concern only the retroactive period and have no stated end; no earlier cessation can be dated, so they are recorded as ending with the express supersession by EO 11812 Sec. 5(3), effective October 1, 1974. The Sec. 1 rates were displaced earlier by EO 11577, but that order's effective date cannot be read in the held text, so the Sec. 1 clauses carry no state yet (see gap) and the whole-order end is not asserted.

original_operative_text:
The incumbent of any position covered 
into the classified civil service of the Gov­
ernment by section 1  of the Executive 
order of April 23, 1941, entitled “Extend­
ing the Classified Civil Service”,1  who, 
between the date of that order and the 
effective date of section 1  thereof, is in­
voluntarily separated from the service by 
reason of a reduction in force, the aboli­
tion of his position, or the liquidation, in 
whole or in part, of the agency in which 
he is employed, may acquire a classified 
civil-service status for transfer to a posi-

tion in the classified civil service: Pro­
vided, (1) that he has rendered six 
months of satisfactory service immedi­
ately prior to his involuntary separation 
from the service; (2) that he is unquali­
fiedly recommended for further Govern­
ment employment by the head of the 
agency in which he last served; (3) that 
he qualifies in such suitable noncompeti­
tive examination as the Civil Service 
Commission may prescribe, only one such 
noncompetitive examination being given 
to any such incumbent; and (4) that he 
obtains such transfer within one year 
from the date of his separation from the 
service.

research_rationale: PARTIAL. EO 8744 (April 24, 1941; 6 FR 2118-2119, held official FR scan text, closing tag '[No. 8744]') has a single operative paragraph: an incumbent of a position covered into the classified service by section 1 of EO 8743 who is involuntarily separated by reduction in force, abolition of the position or liquidation of the agency between the date of EO 8743 and the effective date of its section 1 may acquire a classified status for transfer, provided (among other things) that 'he obtains such transfer within one year from the date of his separation'. By its own terms the authorization could therefore operate only for separations up to the effective date of section 1 of EO 8743 (January 1, 1942 under EO 8743 Sec. 2, earlier for positions that fell vacant after June 30, 1941) and transfers within one year after them. The EO 12608 revocation of September 9, 1987 is a formal cleanup that follows this earlier cessation and is recorded as a later event, not the first end. The exact last day cannot yet be fixed: EO 8743 Sec. 2 was itself amended (EOs 9230, 9358, 9678, 9712 and others touch EO 8743) and it is not established whether any amendment moved the effective date of its section 1; and a transfer deadline is a condition of eligibility, so the date must be fixed from the text, not inferred.

research_rationale: PARTIAL. EO 11911 (April 13, 1976; 41 FR 15683-15684, held official FR scan text) designated the Secretary of the Interior as CITES Management Authority (Secs. 1-2), established the Endangered Species Scientific Authority as Scientific Authority (Sec. 3(a)-(e)), directed a permit system (Sec. 4) and designated the Secretary to act under the Western Hemisphere Convention (Sec. 5). Nine clauses are quoted verbatim; this complete inventory replaces the draft's, whose first two 'clauses' were the file header and the preamble. EO 12608 revoked the order on September 9, 1987 (later event), but that is probably a cleanup: the machine snippet of the 16 U.S.C. 1537a statutory note (the full note was not readable here) says 'but not later than 90 days after Dec. 28, 1979, the functions of the Commission be carried out by the Endangered Species Scientific Authority as established by Ex. Ord. No. 11911', which indicates that Congress replaced the order's Scientific Authority by statute (believed to be Pub. L. 95-632 of 1978 and Pub. L. 96-159 of 1979; unverified). The statute texts are not held, so the first ends of Sec. 3 (and whether Secs. 1, 2, 4 and 5 were displaced by the statutory designation or ran to 1987) are not yet established.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 9883 is a bare revocation with no savings, transition or winding-up clause. EO 9172 itself contains none: it created the National Railway Labor Panel and its emergency boards, which existed only to investigate and report on disputes; reports already made were completed acts, and nothing in either order preserves pending board proceedings, pay or any right. Rail disputes reverted to the Railway Labor Act procedures that EO 9883's recital names as adequate.

research_rationale: EO 9172 (May 22, 1942) created a National Railway Labor Panel 'for the duration of the war and six months thereafter' and let its chairman form three-member emergency boards (paras. 1-3; 7 FR 3913-3914, read in the held govinfo scan). Before taking the revocation as the first end I checked the order's own term: the state of war with Germany and Japan had not been terminated in August 1947 (the President's proclamation of December 31, 1946 ended only hostilities), so the Panel's own term had not run, and EO 9883's recital confirms the Panel still existed. No amendment or partial revocation is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification disposition table, a lead only). EO 9883 (12 FR 5481) revokes the order outright, states no effective date and has no savings clause, so every paragraph ended on its signing date, August 11, 1947. The U.S. Code and eCFR machine searches found no current citation.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 10123 has no savings clause for the Navy organization of EO 9635, which thereafter rested on the statutes (para. 9 itself disclaims any change to the Secretary's statutory authority). Its one qualification is that the revocation 'shall not be construed as reviving' EOs 8984 and 9096, which para. 10 of EO 9635 had revoked. That completed revocation therefore continues, but its continuing basis is EO 10123's non-revival sentence, an independent later source, not EO 9635. No other surviving right, office or obligation of EO 9635 was found.

research_rationale: EO 9635 (September 29, 1945) reorganized the Navy Department in ten numbered paragraphs, read in the held govinfo scan of 10 FR 12419 and its continuation on 12421. It has no expiry or condition of its own. Its main statutory basis, Title I of the First War Powers Act, was by its sec. 401 in force during the war and for six months after its termination; the war had not been terminated by April 1950, and EO 10123 treats the order as still in force, so no earlier statutory lapse is shown. The one earlier event is EO 9904 (November 13, 1947), which replaced the text of para. 8 (order of succession), so the original para. 8 ended on that date. EO 10123 (15 FR 2265) then revoked EO 9635 and EO 9904 without a stated effective date, so every other paragraph ended on its signing date, April 20, 1950, which is the whole-order end. The National Security Act of 1947 and its 1949 amendments, which reorganized the military establishment, were not read here; no held source (OFR catalog, U.S. Code notes, 1989 Codification table) records that they revoked or replaced any paragraph, which is a limit of this bounded search rather than a finding. Savings: EO 10123 keeps EOs 8984 and 9096 revoked (non-revival), an effect now resting on EO 10123. The OFR catalog and the 1989 Codification table (a lead) list no other amendment.

research_rationale: EO 9973 (June 28, 1948; 13 FR 3600, read in the held govinfo scan) has one operative provision: it substitutes subdivision (f) of sec. 6.1 of Civil Service Rule VI of EO 9830 (no removal protection for competitive-status holders of Schedule A or B or statutorily excepted positions, except positions the Commission designates as not confidential or policy-determining). The 1989 Codification table (a lead) and the OFR catalog record its revocation by EO 10577 (1954), but an earlier event ended it: EO 10440 sec. 1 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823) amended Rule VI 'as amended by Executive Order No. 9973' to read as a wholly new Rule VI whose sec. 6.1 has no subdivision (f). EO 10440 states no effective date, so the EO 9973 text ended on March 31, 1953. EO 10577 sec. 301 later revoked EO 9973 by name, effective January 23, 1955 (sec. 401), a formal clean-up of an already displaced amendment, recorded as a later event. No savings preserved the EO 9973 text.

The Commission's schedule placements made under EO 10440 were therefore carried into EO 10577's schedules; they continue, if at all, under EO 10577 and later rules, not under EO 10440. No other savings clause was found.

research_rationale: EO 10440 (March 31, 1953; 18 FR 1823-1824, read in the held govinfo scan) rewrote Civil Service Rule VI (secs. 6.1-6.6, creating Schedule C) and in sec. 2 directed the Commission to reclassify existing Schedule A and B positions, keeping them in place until it acted. Earlier events: EO 10463 (June 25, 1953) replaced sec. 6.4, so the original sec. 6.4 ended that day. The other Rule VI sections continued until EO 10577 sec. 301 revoked EO 10440 by name, effective (sec. 401) on the first Sunday after the sixtieth day after November 22, 1954, i.e. January 23, 1955, which is therefore the whole-order end (no later-ending clause exists). Sec. 2 is a transitional direction that was spent once the Commission had reclassified every listed position; the date that happened is not in the held sources, so its first end is left open rather than set to the revocation date. Savings: EO 10577's proviso carried the schedule listings into the new rules.

EO 10898 itself has no savings provision, and sec. 4 made the Board advisory, without control over any agency, so no agency action depended on it.

research_rationale: EO 10898 (December 2, 1960; 25 FR 12429, read in the held govinfo scan) established the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board of cabinet officers (sec. 1), gave it coordinating and study functions (sec. 2), provided agency assistance (sec. 3), made it advisory only (sec. 4) and required reports (sec. 5). It has no term of its own. Earlier clause-level ends: EO 10986 (January 12, 1962) substituted a new sec. 1(b), so the original membership list ended then; EO 11382 sec. 8 (November 28, 1967) struck all of sec. 1(b) as amended and changed the quorum in sec. 1(d) from three to four, so the original quorum rule ended then. EO 11382 sec. 16(3) also revoked EO 10858, which sec. 4 cites for the President's Committee for Traffic Safety; this is recorded as a later event on sec. 4, but the section's main rule (Board advisory only) continued. EO 11515 (March 13, 1970) terminated the Board and revoked EO 10898 and EO 10986 without a stated effective date, so the remaining clauses ended on March 13, 1970, the whole-order end. The Board consisted of federal officials and ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies.

research_rationale: EO 10986 (January 12, 1962; 27 FR 439-440, read in the held govinfo scan) has one operative provision: it substitutes a new sec. 1(b) of EO 10898, adding the Secretary of Labor to the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board. The 1989 Codification table (a lead) and the OFR catalog record its revocation by EO 11515 in 1970, but an earlier event ended its text: EO 11382 sec. 8 (November 28, 1967) amended EO 10898 'as amended' by striking out all of sec. 1(b) and inserting a new list headed by the Secretary of Transportation. EO 11382 states no effective date, so the EO 10986 list ended on November 28, 1967. EO 11515's revocation (March 13, 1970) is recorded as a later formal clean-up.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Section 1(a)  . "There is hereby established the Interagency Commit­
tee on International Athletics. The Committee shall collect, exchange, 
and review information concerning amateur athletic matters that 
might tend to affect the foreign relations or general welfare of the 
United States. The Committee shall be composed of representatives 
to be designated by the Secretary of State, the Attorney General, the 
Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare (in his capacity as 
Chairman of the President’s Council on Physical Fitness), and the 
heads of such other departments and agencies as the President may 
from time to time designate, dr as may be invited to participate in 
the activities of the Committee upon its request. The head of each 
department or agency represented on the Committee shall designate 
one or more alternates. The representative of the Department of State 
shall serve as chairman of the Committee.

research_rationale: EO 11117 (August 13, 1963; 28 FR 8397-8398, read in the held govinfo scan) established an Interagency Committee on International Athletics of agency representatives, with information-gathering and reporting functions (secs. 1-3). It has no term or condition of its own, no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead), and it ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies. EO 11515 sec. 2 terminated the Committee and revoked EO 11117 without a stated effective date, so every clause ended on March 13, 1970.

research_rationale: EO 11152 (April 15, 1964; 29 FR 5271-5272, read in the held govinfo scan) established the President's Committee on Manpower of cabinet and agency heads to assist the Secretary of Labor under the Manpower Development and Training Act (secs. 1-4). It has no term or condition of its own, no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead), and it ended before the Federal Advisory Committee Act (1972) existed, so no statutory termination applies. EO 11515 sec. 3 terminated the Committee and revoked EO 11152 without a stated effective date, so every clause ended on March 13, 1970. Winding up went to the Bureau of the Budget (sec. 6).

Committee on the Status o f Women (hereinafter referred to as the

who shall be the Chairman o f the Committee, the Secretary o f State, 
the Secretary o f Defense, the Attorney General, the Secretary of 
Agriculture, the Secretary o f Commerce, the Secretary o f Health, 
Education, and W elfare, and the Chairman of the Civil Service Com­
mission, all ex officio. The Director o f the Women’s Bureau o f the 
Department o f Labor shall serve as Executive Vice-Chairman o f the 
Committee, and shall be an ex officio member thereof.

research_rationale: EO 11126 (November 1, 1963; 28 FR 11717-11718, read in the held govinfo scan) set up an Interdepartmental Committee on the Status of Women of cabinet officers (Part I) and a Citizens' Advisory Council on the Status of Women (Part II), with support provisions (Part III). It has no term of its own. Clause-level history: EO 11221 (May 6, 1965) substituted new texts for secs. 101(a), 103 and 201, so the original texts ended then. The Council was an advisory committee in existence on January 5, 1973 and would have expired under sec. 14(a)(1) of the Federal Advisory Committee Act on January 5, 1975, but EO 11827 (signed January 4, 1975) continued it to January 5, 1977 and EO 11948 (effective December 31, 1976) to December 31, 1978, so there was no statutory lapse. EO 12007 (August 22, 1977) terminated the Council and revoked sec. 102(5) and Part II and rewrote sec. 103 and the second sentence of sec. 301, so those clauses ended then. The Committee clauses (federal officials, outside the Act) continued until EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11126 as amended, signed April 4, 1978 with no other effective date stated: that is the whole-order end. None of these orders contains a savings clause.

unresolved_material_gaps: Public Law 94-167 (89 Stat. 1003), the statute under which the Commission operated after 1975, is not held and was not read; its duration and termination terms decide when the Commission clauses (secs. 1(a), 1(c), 1(d), 2(a)-(g), 3) ended (on or before April 4, 1978).
Sec. 4 interdepartmental task force for International Women's Year: date on which it was spent or ended not established (no later than April 4, 1978, EO 12050).
whole_order_end not set: depends on the two items above; EO 12050 sec. 8 (signed April 4, 1978) is the latest possible date, not a confirmed first end.
savings_residuals not closed: EO 12050 has no savings clause, but whether Public Law 94-167 preserved or transferred any Commission function or report duty has not been read.
research_rationale: EO 11832 (January 9, 1975; 40 FR 2415-2417, read in the held govinfo scan) established the National Commission on the Observance of International Women's Year, 1975 (secs. 1-3) and an interdepartmental task force (sec. 4). Exact clause-level ends found: EO 11889 (November 25, 1975) replaced the original sec. 2(h), which had ended the Commission's work with 1975; EO 11979 (March 28, 1977) replaced the original sec. 1(b) membership rule (further amended by EO 11980). The other clauses are certainly terminated by the cutoff, since EO 12050 sec. 8 revoked EO 11832 as amended on April 4, 1978, but that revocation may be a clean-up. Under EO 11889 the Commission was to end after a final report due within thirty days after June 30, 1976. EO 11979 shows it was still operating in 1977 'in accord with Section 2' of Public Law 94-167, which directed it to organize the National Women's Conference, and the Commission was set up after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect, so sec. 14(a)(2) of that Act also bears on its duration. Without reading Public Law 94-167, which states how long the Commission lasted and when it ended, the first ends of the Commission and task-force clauses, the whole-order end and the savings question cannot be fixed honestly; they are left open.

research_rationale: EO 11534 (June 4, 1970; 35 FR 8865, read in the held govinfo scan) created a National Council on Organized Crime of eighteen named federal officials to formulate a national strategy against organized crime. It has no term, report deadline or condition, and no amendment is recorded (OFR catalog; 1989 Codification table, a lead). EO 12110 sec. 1-103(c) lists it among orders 'that established committees which have terminated or whose work is completed'. That recital gives no date and is not itself a legal act ending the Council earlier; the order's own terms set no end, and the Council, composed wholly of full-time federal officers, was outside the termination rule of sec. 14 of the Federal Advisory Committee Act (the continuance orders EO 11827 and EO 11948 accordingly do not list it). The legal first end of every clause is therefore the revocation, effective December 31, 1978 under sec. 1-105. Changes in some members' offices (for example the Post Office Department and the Bureau of Narcotics and Dangerous Drugs were later reorganized) altered who sat on the Council but did not end it; they were not separately researched.

The Committee (ten labor and ten management members appointed by the President) was created April 1, 1975, after the Federal Advisory Committee Act took effect; under its sec. 14(a)(2) (held 86 Stat. 776) such a committee terminates not later than two years after establishment unless renewed. EO 11948 (effective 1976-12-31), the general continuance order, did not renew it, and EO 12110 sec. 1-103(b) describes it as terminated or its work completed. Whether the Act applied and whether any separate renewal was made has not been established, so the expiry date (about April 1, 1977) is not asserted.

research_rationale: EO 11849 (April 1, 1975; 40 FR 14887-14888, read in the held govinfo scan) created the Collective Bargaining Committee in Construction (secs. 1-6). The order has no term of its own. EO 12110 sec. 1-103(b) revoked it effective December 31, 1978 as one whose committee had 'terminated' or whose work was 'completed', which signals an earlier end. The likely earlier end is the two-year limit of Federal Advisory Committee Act sec. 14(a)(2), since the general continuance order of December 1976 (EO 11948) did not renew it. Because the Act's application and the absence of any other renewal are not proven from held sources, first ends and the whole-order end are left open. Savings: none found. The U.S. Code note (29 U.S.C. 171 note) and the eCFR hits are historical and report the revocation; no CONFLICT is open.

unresolved_material_gaps: Actual date of submission of the Committee's report (due no later than June 11, 1977 under EO 11982) and any presidential extension under sec. 3(b) not established; the Committee terminated thirty days after submission unless extended, so the first end of the clauses tied to its existence cannot be dated. A deadline does not prove the report date. EO 12110 (effective 1978-12-31) describes the Committee as terminated or its work completed.
whole_order_end not set until the report and extension question is resolved (latest possible date 1978-12-31).
research_rationale: EO 11971 (February 11, 1977; 42 FR 9155-9156, read in the held govinfo scan) created a temporary Committee on Selection of the Director of the FBI (secs. 1-7). Sec. 3(b) makes it terminate thirty days after it submits its report unless the President extends it. EO 11982 (April 29, 1977) replaced the original sec. 3(a), so that clause's first end is exact. All other clauses depended on the Committee's existence, which ended under the order's own terms at a date not recorded in held sources, or, if extended, no later than EO 12110's revocation effective December 31, 1978. EO 12110 itself describes the Committee as terminated or its work completed. Those first ends and the whole-order end are left open rather than inferred from the June 11, 1977 deadline. Savings: none found.

(b) The Commission shall identify, study, and make recommendations on critical 
military compensation issues, specifically addressing the following issues:
( 1  ) What form of military compensation is the most effective for meeting the 
needs of the Nation in peace and war? Is the present pay and allowances system ap­
propriate? If not, what changes (such as some form of military salary) offer greater 
potential to serve the national purpose?

military compensation? If so, what should the standards be? What elements of com­
pensation should be based on such standards?
(3) What provisions are appropriate for differential compensation (such as spe­
cial and incentive pays) and what are the appropriate criteria for using them?
(4) What are the purposes of the military retirement system? Is the present system 
effective in achieving these purposes? What changes are appropriate?
(5) Should the unique characteristics of military service be reflected in the com­
pensation system, and, if so, how?

unresolved_material_gaps: Exact first end of the clauses that lasted until the revocation not established: EO 9687 (signed January 26, 1946; 11 FR 1033) revoked the order but 'shall become effective with respect to any agency concerned as of the close of its pay period terminating or current on January 31, 1946'. The effective date therefore differs by agency (January 31, 1946, or the later close of a pay period current on that day), so no single exact date can be asserted for those clauses or for the whole order.

EO 9449 (effective July 1, 1944) made no losses payable to most War and Navy Department personnel and by its sec. 2 amended 'accordingly' every conflicting provision of EO 7972 as amended; how far that implied amendment ended the clauses marked with the EO 9449 later event has not been delimited.

savings_residuals not closed: EO 9687 has no savings clause; whether claims for currency-appreciation losses that accrued before each agency's effective date remained payable (accrued rights under the Act of March 26, 1934, as amended) has not been established.
research_rationale: EO 7972 (September 15, 1938; 3 FR 2249-2252, read in the held govinfo scan) prescribed regulations for paying currency-appreciation losses of officers, enlisted men and employees serving abroad (secs. 1-7), with a table of basic rates in sec. 4. It was amended by EOs 8018 (new sec. 3(h)), 8261 (additions to sec. 1(b); new sec. 2(b)), 8269 (complete new rate table, effective December 1, 1939), 8800, 9057 and 9261 (table entries) and 9449 (new sec. 2(b) and conflict amendment, effective July 1, 1944), and was revoked with all of them by EO 9687. Exact clause-level ends: the original sec. 2(b) ended September 21, 1939 (EO 8261) and the original rate table December 1, 1939 (EO 8269). The other clauses lasted until EO 9687, whose effective date is set agency by agency at the close of the pay period terminating or current on January 31, 1946, so no single exact date can be asserted. EO 9449's conflict amendment also cut back several clauses for War and Navy personnel from July 1, 1944, to an extent not delimited here. Sec. 7's supersession of EO 6928 was a one-time disposition; EO 9687 does not say whether its revocation revives earlier orders, and none was found to have been revived. The first ends, whole-order end and savings are left open.

No later order replaced sec. 3(h). July 9, 1932
Executive Order
FURTHER TEMPORARY EXEMPTION OF CERTAIN PERSONS FROM COMPUL-
SORY RETIREMENT FOR AGE IN ORDER TO AFFORD
TIME FOR FILLING VACANCIES
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 204 of Part II of the act
entitled " AN ACT Making appropriations for the Legislative Branch of the Govern-
ment for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1933, and for other purposes ," approved
June 30 , 1932, the following-named persons who have reached the retirement age
prescribed for automatic separation from the service and who were temporarily
exempted from the provisions of that section and continued in the service until July
10 , 1932, by Executive order dated June 30 , 1932 (No. 5874), are hereby further
temporarily exempted from the provisions of that section and continued in the service
until August 1, 1932 :
Name
William L.

entitled " AN ACT Making appropriations for the Legislative Branch of the Govern-
ment for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1933, and for other purposes ," approved
June 30 , 1932, the following-named persons who have reached the retirement age
prescribed for automatic separation from the service and who were temporarily
exempted from the provisions of that section and continued in the service until July
10 , 1932, by Executive order dated June 30 , 1932 (No. 5874), are hereby further

William L. Hill
John Lewis May
Leonard Magruder
Department
Treasury"
"
These persons hold positions which the public interest requires be continuously
filled , and the additional temporary exemptions herein granted are for such period
only as is absolutely necessary to afford time in which to appoint successors to the
present incumbents of these positions .

research_rationale:
EO 5881 (July 9, 1932), read in the official OFR 1974 Hoover PEO vol. II compilation (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original), is a single-clause order under section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 further exempting William L. Hill, John Lewis May and Leonard Magruder (Treasury) from compulsory retirement 'and continued in the service until August 1, 1932', to afford time to appoint successors. It follows the earlier exemption order of June 30, 1932 recited in its text (whose exemption ran to July 10, 1932; that order's number is not in the project's identity universe, so it is not cited by number here). The order ends by its own terms on 1932-08-01. NOTE: the machine TERM record's stated_end_date (1932-07-10) misreads the recital of the earlier order's term; its span (chars 910-1759 of the held text) contains the operative words 'until August 1, 1932', which govern. Authority check: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (Economy Act). No held source shows repeal or amendment of section 204 before this order's stated end date; the held WPA entries for EO 6615 (Feb. 26, 1934) and EO 6974/6975 (Feb. 1935) show the President still granting exemptions from the compulsory retirement provisions after this order's end, which corroborates that the statutory scheme (and so the exemption's object) continued through the stated date.

Executive Order 5982. December 22, 1932
Executive Order
EXEMPTION OF CHARLES J. HARLOW FROM COMPULSORY RETIREMENT
FOR AGE
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 204 of Part II of the act
entitled " AN ACT Making appropriations for the Legislative Branch of the Govern-
ment for the fiscal year ending June 30 , 1933 , and for other purposes ," approved June
30 , 1932, Charles J. Harlow, plate printer in the Coast and Geodetic Survey of the
Department of Commerce , who, during the current month , reaches the retirement
age prescribed for automatic separation from the service , is hereby exempted from the
provisions of that section until March 31 , 1933 .

research_rationale:
EO 5982 (Dec. 22, 1932), read in the official OFR 1974 Hoover PEO vol. II compilation (official_compilation_high, acceptable_as_original), exempts Charles J. Harlow, plate printer in the Coast and Geodetic Survey, from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 'until March 31, 1933'. Single time-limited grant ending by its own terms on 1933-03-31. The held OCR text omits the signature line; the compilation page, not the OCR, is the original, and the operative text is complete. Authority check: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (Economy Act). No held source shows repeal or amendment of section 204 before this order's stated end date; the held WPA entries for EO 6615 (Feb. 26, 1934) and EO 6974/6975 (Feb. 1935) show the President still granting exemptions from the compulsory retirement provisions after this order's end, which corroborates that the statutory scheme (and so the exemption's object) continued through the stated date.

Executive Order 5707. September 4, 1931
Executive Order
Amendments to Regulations Governing the Occupation and
Maintenance of Certain Foreign Service Quarters
The following changes are authorized in the regulations established by Executive
Order No. 5624, dated May 15 , 1931 , governing the occupation and maintenance of
diplomatic or consular residential and office quarters owned or leased for long terms
by the United States :
(a) The phrase " in the quarters used for residence purposes " is added to the
end of section 15 .
(b) Section 20 is amended to read as follows :
20. The Department of State will bear the cost of renewing and repairing office
furniture and the cost of ordinary and periodical cleaning , including the beating of
carpets , the cleaning or washing of curtains , etc. , used in the offices; but the cost of
ordinary and periodical cleaning, including the beating of carpets , the cleaning or
washing of curtains , etc. , in the quarters used for residence purposes must be borne
by the officer personally .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
September 4, 1931 .
HERBERT HOOVER
[No. 5707]

research_rationale:
Original: EO 5707 of September 4, 1931, read in full in the official OFR 1974 Hoover PEO vol. II, printed p. 993 (PDF p. 222): it authorizes two changes to the Foreign Service quarters regulations of EO 5624 — (a) adds 'in the quarters used for residence purposes' to section 15, and (b) rewrites section 20 (the three inventory scopes cover (a), the (b) instruction and the new section 20 text). Ending: EO 8189 of July 5, 1939 (4 FR 2783, held govinfo FR PDF text), 'Revocation of Executive Orders: The following executive orders are hereby revoked: ... Executive Order No. 5624 dated May 15, 1931; Executive Order No. 5707 dated September 4, 1931; ...'. EO 8189 states no effective date of its own (the 'effective July 1, 1939' sentences on the same FR page belong to EOs 8190 and 8191), so it took effect on signing, July 5, 1939 (filed July 6, 1939). The actor is EO 8189; the dossier's duplicate ACT records for EOs 8190-8192 point at the same page and were not used.

Executive Order 5614. May 1 , 1931
Executive Order
Reporting of Expenditures for Use in the Budget
In pursuance of the provisions of the Budget and Accounting Act approved
June 10 , 1921 , I hereby prescribe the following rules and regulations with regard
to the reporting of expenditures in the Budget :
1. As soon as practicable after the close of each fiscal year, the Secretary of the
Treasury shall furnish the Director of the Bureau of the Budget with a detailed
statement of the expenditures of the Government on the basis of checks issued by
disbursing officers and agents of the United States , under each separate head of
appropriations as carried on the books of the Treasury Department ; and such
expenditures shall be classified separately under the captions " General fund,"
"Special funds ," and " Trust funds ," respectively .
2. In order to enable the Secretary of the Treasury to comply with the provisions
of this order , the head of each executive department and independent establishment
shall furnish the Secretary of the Treasury as soon as practicable after the close of
each fiscal year with a detailed statement of the unexpended balances in the hands of
disbursing officers and agents , or to their official credit, at the close of the fiscal year
for which such report is made , classified according to appropriations , special funds ,
trust funds , and special deposit accounts as carried on the books of the Treasury .
3. The Secretary of the Treasury shall prescribe such forms as he may consider
necessary to carry out the provisions of this order .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
May 1 , 1931 .
HERBERT HOOVER
[No. 5614]

source.quote:
]Executive 1t'rer
As an evidence of the profound affection of the American people
for the memory of Abraham Lincoln, it is hereby ordered that the
executive offices of the United States shall be closed and that the national
flag be displayed at half-mast upon all Federal buildings and at all forts
and military posts and naval stations and on all vessels of the United
States, and that the representatives of the United States in foreign coun-
tries shall in like manner pay appropriate tribute to his memory, on
Thursday, April 15, 1915, the fiftieth anniversary of his death.
The owners and masters of all merchant ships of the United States
are requested similarly to display the national flag at half-mast.
WOODROW WILSON
THE WHITE HOUSE,
13 April, 1915.
[No. 2171.]

The dossier holds no own-terms record for this order, so the end cites the order's complete held text, which contains the stated day.

EO 2171 (April 13, 1915, Woodrow Wilson), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan text (jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_2171.txt; grade archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held) and checked against the page image I rendered on 2026-10-28 from the held PDF ('ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1915-EO-2171.pdf', sha256 6887d229..., equal to the registry's; one page; heading 'Executive Order', signature 'WOODROW WILSON', date '13 April, 1915', printed '[No. 2171.]', handwritten '2171' at top). The OCR layer is complete; its first line (']Executive 1t'rer') is the misread heading 'Executive Order', not order text. The order directs that the executive offices of the United States be closed, that the national flag be displayed at half-mast on all Federal buildings, forts, military posts, naval stations and vessels of the United States, and that the representatives of the United States in foreign countries pay tribute in like manner, 'on Thursday, April 15, 1915, the fiftieth anniversary of his death' (Abraham Lincoln's). Its second paragraph only requests owners and masters of merchant ships to display the flag at half-mast; a request is not a command. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the scan, the registry record (signing date 1915-04-13) and the census register. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1915-04-15, the only day it governs; a reader who dates cessation to the first day without effect would write 1915-04-16, and this claim records 1915-04-15, the day through whose end the order ran, consistent with the owner's inclusive reading of stated dates. Searches made on 2026-10-28: census register titles and the WPA 1944 numbered list for 1915 Lincoln or half-mast orders, and a citation search of every held order text for 'No. 2171' and 'Order No. 2171'. The only citation hit, in jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_7870.txt, amends an 'Administrative Order No. 2171', a different instrument. Nothing names EO 2171. The machine USC and eCFR searches (complete, 0 hits) exclude a current-law reference; the OFR catalog search starts in 1937 and is not relied on alone.

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 6702—Exemption of Herman M. Underwood from Compulsory Retirement for Age; May 07, 1934; APP node 362475; common-crawl capture 2025-11-10T10:42:08Z
source.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404; 5 U.S.C., sec. 692b), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *."

And Whereas the public interest requires that Herman M. Underwood, associate engineer in the Engineer Department at Large, War Department, Newark, New Jersey, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until October 1, 1934;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Herman M. Underwood from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until October 1, 1934.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

May 7, 1934.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms: exempts the employee 'until November 1, 1935'. Recorded as 1935-11-01, inclusive; exclusive alternative stated in the rationale.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires: * * *."

And Whereas the public interest requires that James S. Goldsmith, superintendent of buildings and labor of the United States National Museum, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 1 year by Executive Order No. 6338, dated October 14, 1933, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until November 1, 1935:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby further exempt James S. Goldsmith from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until November 1, 1935.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 6920—Excusing Federal Employees From Duty at 1 P.M. on December 24 and at 1 P.M. on December 31, 1934; December 13, 1934; APP node 373460; common-crawl capture 2025-11-16T19:45:19Z
source.quote:
It is hereby ordered that the several executive departments, independent establishments and other government agencies in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, be closed at 1 P.M. on Monday, December 24, 1934, the day preceding Christmas Day, and at 1 P.M. on Monday, December 31, 1934, the day preceding New Year's Day, and that all employees in the Federal service in the District of Columbia, and in the field service of the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies of the Government, except those who may for special public reasons be excluded from the provisions of this Order by the heads of their respective departments, establishments or agencies, or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent with the provisions of existing law, are hereby excused from duty at 1 P.M. on Monday, December 24, 1934, and at 1 P.M. on Monday, December 31, 1934.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

December 13, 1934.

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Andre Fourchy from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until January 1, 1937.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

December 10, 1935.

AND WHEREAS the public interest requires that André Fourchy, associate civil engineer, United States Coast Guard, Treasury Department, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of one year by Executive Order No. 7248 of December 10, 1935, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until January 1, 1938;

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt André Fourchy from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until January 1, 1938.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

THE WHITE HOUSE,

December 16, 1936.

EO 254 (February 18, 1904, Theodore Roosevelt), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image I rendered on 2026-10-28 from the held PDF ('ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1904-EO-254.pdf', sha256 63a96efb..., the registered source hash; one page). The image shows the heading 'EXECUTIVE ORDER.', one sentence, the signature 'THEODORE ROOSEVELT.' and 'White House, February 18, 1904.'; it bears no printed order number. Identity rests on the ProQuest record 1904-EO-254, the census register row EO:254 (1904, ProQuest) and the WPA 1944 numbered list entry No. 254 (February 18, 1904: 'Federal offices in Ohio ordered closed Feb. 19, 1904, for funeral services of Marcus A. Hanna'), which agree with the text. The OCR layer is badly degraded ('monory' for memory, 'sours' for hours, 'ninetoenth inetant' for nineteenth instant, 'THEOTORE'); the page image reads: 'As a mark of respect to the memory of Hon. Marcus A. Hanna, late Senator of the United States from the State of Ohio, it is hereby ordered that all Federal offices in Ohio be closed during the hours of the funeral to-morrow, Friday, the nineteenth instant.' Inventory correction: the dossier's machine clause span (characters 580-685) is OCR noise from the blank lower page; the corrected scope EO:254#corrected-1 covers characters 163-565 of the held text, from the heading through the date line. The type label office_closing_mourning fits. First end: by its own terms on 1904-02-19, the only day it governs; the closing ran only during the funeral hours that day, so the order had no operation after that day. February 19, 1904 was a Friday, consistent with 'to-morrow, Friday' written on February 18. The hour the funeral ended is not held and does not affect the recorded date. Searches on 2026-10-28: the WPA 1944 list and census titles for Hanna (no other entry concerns Senator Hanna's death or funeral); a full-text search of every held order text for 'Hanna' with 'funeral' (only this order); a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 254' (only navigation links in the Wikisource pages for EO 253 and EO 255).

Executive Order
CHRISTMAS , 1931
It is hereby ordered that the several executive departments and independent
Government establishments in the District of Columbia , including the Government
Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, be closed on Saturday, December
26 , 1931 , and all clerks and other employees in the Federal service in the District
of Columbia, except those who may for special public reasons be excepted from the

with the provisions of existing law, are hereby excused from duty on that day.
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
December 22 , 1931 .

Executive Order 5763. December 22, 1931
Executive Order
CHRISTMAS , 1931
It is hereby ordered that the several executive departments and independent
Government establishments in the District of Columbia , including the Government
Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, be closed on Saturday, December
26 , 1931 , and all clerks and other employees in the Federal service in the District
of Columbia, except those who may for special public reasons be excepted from the
provisions of this order, or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent
with the provisions of existing law, are hereby excused from duty on that day.
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
December 22 , 1931 .
[No. 5763]

The registered APP transcription (mirror_transcription) agrees with the granting sentence word for word, prints the second name as 'Jacob L. N uber', and passed the APP page check. Later orders naming it, recorded as later events with their own dates and quotes: EO 6615 (February 26, 1934) recites that Nuber 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 1 year by Executive Order No. 6013, dated February 3, 1933' and further exempts him until February 28, 1935; EO 6974 (February 21, 1935) recites EO 6013 and EO 6615 ('two periods of 1 year each') and further exempts Nuber until March 1, 1936. FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 6615—Exemption of Jacob L. Nuber from Compulsory Retirement for Age; February 26, 1934; APP node 362384; common-crawl capture 2025-11-06T23:33:31Z
source.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404; 5 U.S.C., sec. 692b), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires:"

And Whereas the public interest requires that Jacob L. Nuber, Chief of the Printing and Binding Section, Bureau of Internal Revenue, Treasury Department, who was 70 years of age on February 26, 1933, and who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 1 year by Executive Order No. 6013, dated February 3, 1933, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until February 28, 1935;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid statute, I do hereby exempt Jacob L. Nuber from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until February 28, 1935.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

February 26, 1934.

Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404; U.S.C., title 5, sec. 692b), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this, section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires: * * * ";

And Whereas the public interest requires that David E. Roberts, Assistant Chief, Division of Fine Arts, Library of Congress, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 2 years by Executive Order No. 6106, dated April 10, 1933, be further exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until May 1, 1937;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt David E. Roberts from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until May 1, 1937.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

April 10, 1935.

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 7122—Exemption of Mrs. Frances N. Westcott From Compulsory Retirement for Age; July 31, 1935; APP node 376535; common-crawl capture 2025-09-07T10:33:30Z
source.quote:
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, ch. 314, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C., sec. 692b), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires *** ";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Mrs. Frances N. Westcott, Attendant, Senate Office Building, who during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until January 1, 1936:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Mrs. Frances N. Westcott from the provisions thereof and continue her in the service until January 1, 1936.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

July 31, 1935.

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Frederick D. Henry, Chief Clerk, Freedmen's Hospital, Department of the Interior, who, during the current month, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until December 1, 1936.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

source.page_or_item: Executive Order 7249—Excusing Federal Employees from Duty at 1 p.m. on December 24 and 31, 1935; December 12, 1935; APP node 362747; common-crawl capture 2025-09-16T13:28:15Z
source.quote:
By virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me as President of the United States, it is hereby ordered that the several executive departments, independent establishments and other governmental agencies in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, be closed at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 24, 1935, the day preceding Christmas Day, and at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 31, 1935, the day preceding New Year's Day; and ajl employees in the Federal service in the District of Columbia, and in the field service of the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies of the Government, except those who may for special public reasons be excluded from the provisions of this Order by the heads of their respective departments, establishments or agencies, or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent with the provisions of existing law, are hereby excused from duty at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 24, 1935, and at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 31, 1935.

For the purposes of this Order, in establishments or agencies in which the employees work in shifts, such employees shall, subject to the foregoing provisions, be excused from duty after four hours of work on the dates specified, and the several shifts shall be arranged accordingly.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

December 12, 1935.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by its own terms at the close of Tuesday, December 31, 1935, the second of the two half-day closings ('at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 24, 1935 ... and at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 31, 1935'). Actor: EO 7249 itself. The dossier's only own-terms record is the undated shift condition, so the end cites the order's complete registered text, which contains the stated dates.

EO 7249 (December 12, 1935, Franklin D. Roosevelt). Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming EO 7249, its date (December 12, 1935) appears in the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. It closes the executive departments, independent establishments and other agencies in the District of Columbia, including the Government Printing Office and the Navy Yard and stations, at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 24, 1935 and at 1 P.M. on Tuesday, December 31, 1935, and excuses employees in the District and in the field service from duty at those hours, except those excluded by their agency heads for special public reasons or whose absence would be inconsistent with existing law. A second paragraph applies the order to shift workers, who are excused 'after four hours of work on the dates specified'. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page, the census register (1935-12-12) and the WPA 1944 list ('Federal offices ordered closed at 1 p. m. on Dec. 24 and 31, 1935'). The type label office_closing_mourning fits. First end: by its own terms at the close of 1935-12-31, the second and last day it governs (the December 24 part was spent at the close of that day). Both days were Tuesdays, as the order says. The dossier's own-terms record for the shift paragraph is classed as a condition with no date; the condition is tied to 'the dates specified' and adds no later date. Searches on 2026-10-28: the WPA 1944 list and census titles for Christmas and late-December closings 1931-1936 (EO 7499 of November 27, 1936, for December 24 and 26, 1936, is a new order for another year and does not name EO 7249), and a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 7249' (only navigation links in Wikisource pages for adjacent numbers); nothing names EO 7249.
