research_rationale: EO 11737 (signed 1973-09-07, 38 FR 24883-24884), read in full from the held official FR text, enlarges the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission: Sec. 1 amends EO 11659 (new Secs. 2, 3(3) and 5, a new Sec. 6 and redesignation of Sec. 6 as Sec. 7); Sec. 2 transfers the terminated Souris-Red-Rainy commission's assets and obligations to it; Sec. 3 supersedes EO 11359 and EO 11635. The Sec. 1 text was never amended by a later order (later amendments of EO 11659 by EO 11882, 12038 and 12148 touch only Sec. 3(2)) and ended when EO 12319 sec. 1(f) terminated the commission on December 31, 1981, which is the whole-order end; EO 12319 sec. 5(b) then revoked EO 11659 'as amended' effective January 1, 1982, attached as a later event. Secs. 2 and 3 are one-time commands completed on taking effect on 1973-09-07. Dossier gap 'target provision not located: EO:12319' is resolved by reading EO 12319 in the held official FR text, whose Sec. 1 and Sec. 5 were page-checked against the official issue PDF (PAGECHK3, PDF pages 7-8, FR 45591-45592). Bounded search: EO 11659 and every amending order in its chain (EO 11737, 11882, 12038, 12148), and EO 12319 read in full from the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of the held FR-original texts finds '11737' only in its own text; OFR catalog, U.S. Code and eCFR machine searches (2 OFR catalog hits, the amendment and revocation notes of EO 11659; 0 U.S. Code and 0 eCFR hits for this order). This claim's first ends do not depend on how the replaced original Secs. 2, 3(3) and 5 of EO 11659 are read (that strike-and-reinsert question belongs to the EO 11659 claim). No report deadline or transcription copy question is needed. AI producer hypothesis only; no human certification is asserted.

savings_residuals.reason: EO 11737 has no savings wording of its own. Its Sec. 2 moved the Souris-Red-Rainy commission's funds, property, records, employees, assets and obligations into the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission, so those items became that commission's assets and obligations. On the commission's termination, EO 12319 (official FR, page-checked) sec. 2 provides for an orderly close-out with optional transition of commission activities to the member States, and sec. 3 directs that commission assets the Federal Government might otherwise claim be transferred to the member States (or entities they designate), subject to OMB approval of the terms. The residual assets are therefore transferred, not continued under this order; nothing of EO 11737 remains operative.

research_rationale: EO 8427 (signed 1940-06-03, 5 FR 2131), read in full from the held official FR text: enacting words under Reorganization Plan No. IV of 1940 and secs. 1-8 governing the Interbuilding Mail and Messenger Service. The dossier's 8 clauses cover secs. 1-8 with no operative gap (the text before sec. 1 is the enacting recital). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:8427>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own: sec. 8 ('This order shall become effective upon the effective date of the said Reorganization Plan No. IV') is a start, not an end, and the sec. 4 'Unless otherwise directed' wording (the dossier's machine own-term tags) is a condition of service, not an end. The by-number scan finds 8427 only in EO 12553 (its own number line '[No. 84271' aside); the OFR catalog records only the EO 12553 revocation; no held order names the Official Mail and Messenger Service or the interbuilding mail service. Non-express lead only, not an end: the Post Office Department, in which sec. 1 placed the service, was replaced by the United States Postal Service under the Postal Reorganization Act of 1970 (statute not held; it names no executive order and no held instrument or OFR note says it acted on EO 8427). The order is therefore recorded as ending at its first express end, EO 12553, which the President described as eliminating orders 'no longer necessary'; this is not proof of continuous operation to 1986. Ended with the whole order: first end EO 12244, 1981-10-01. later_events.mechanism: formal revocation after the end: express revocation by EO 12553 ('it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:', followed by the table row 12244 'Providing exemption for Fort Allen from compliance with the Federal Water Pollution Control Act'); EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation took effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986); the exemptions had already expired on 1981-10-01, so this clears a spent order and does not move the first end

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of  
the United States of America, including Section 313 of the Federal W ater  
Pollution Control Act, as amended (33 U .S .C . 1323), Section 118 of the Clean  
Air Act, as amended (42 U .S .C . 7418), Section 4 of the Noise Control A ct of  
1972 (42 U .S .C . 4903), and Section 6001 of the Solid Waste Disposal A ct, as  
amended (42 U .S .C . 6961), and in order to provide for the immediate relocation  
and temporary housing of Haitian and Cuban nationals, who are located in the  
State of Florida and presently in the custody of the United States, at a Federal  
facility known as Fort Allen, located in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico,  
and having determined it to be in the paramount interest of the United States  
to exempt Fort Allen from all the requirements otherwise imposed on it by the  
said statutes, it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-101. Consistent with the provisions of Subsection (a) of Section 313 of the  
Federal Water Pollution Control A ct, as amended (33 U .S .C . 1323(a)), each and  
every effluent source located at Fort Allen is exempted from compliance with  
the provisions of that Act; except that no exemption is hereby granted from  
Sections 306 and 307 of that A ct (33 U .S .C . 1316 and 1317).
1-102. Consistent with the provisions of subsection (b) of Section 118 of the  
Clean Air Act, as amended (42 U .S .C . 7418(b)), each and every particular  
emission source located at Fort Allen is exempted from compliance with the  
provisions of that Act; except that no exemption is hereby granted from  
Sections 111 and 112 of that A ct (42 U .S .C . 7411 and 7412).
1-103. Consistent with the provisions of subsection 4(b) of the Noise Control  
A ct of 1972, as amended (42 U .S .C . 4903(b)), each and every single activity or  
facility, including noise emission sources or classes thereof, located at Fort  
Allen, are exempted from compliance with the provisions of that Act; except  
that no exemption is hereby granted from Sections 6,17 and 18 of that A ct (42  
U .S .C . 4906, 4916 and 4917).
1-104. Consistent with the provisions of Section 6001 of the Solid W aste  
Disposal Act, as amended (42 U .S .C . 6961), each and every solid waste  
management facility located at Fort Allen is exempted from compliance with  
the provision  of that Act.
1-105. The exemptions granted by this Order shall be for the one-year period  
beginning October 2,1980, and ending October 1,1981.

research_rationale: EO 12244 (signed 1980-10-03, 45 FR 66443), read in full from the held official FR text: enacting words, secs. 1-101 to 1-104 (four statutory exemptions for Fort Allen) and sec. 1-105 (one-year period ending October 1, 1981). The dossier's single clause covers the whole operative text. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:12244>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order's own sec. 1-105 limits every exemption to the one-year period ending October 1, 1981; that is a fixed date, not a report deadline. The by-number scan finds 12244 only in EO 12553 (the EO 11557 hit is an FR document number); 'Fort Allen' appears in held texts only in EO 12244, EO 12246 and EO 12251 (Cuban-Haitian entrant assistance lists, which neither extend nor change the exemptions), EO 12327 (the separate exemption for the next year, read in full: it does not name EO 12244) and EO 12553; the OFR catalog records only the EO 12553 revocation for EO 12244. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is therefore only an upper bound: the first end is the 1981-10-01 expiry, and EO 12553 is attached as a later event. First end: EO 12244, 1981-10-01. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, text_sha256 6361bdc5..., 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15, read for this purpose: heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966 and the signature block): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording anywhere in the held text (searched saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that). Own-residual check, reading EO 12244 in full: it granted time-limited statutory exemptions to Fort Allen; it created no office, fund, property or private right, and the exemptions expired on 1981-10-01 under sec. 1-105. Conduct during the exempt year was a completed matter; the next year's exemption rests on EO 12327, not on EO 12244. EO 12553 has no savings clause. Nothing of the order outlived 1981-10-01. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); a subject-word scan of the same texts; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

THE PRESIDENT 10737
Executive Order 11541
PRESCRIBING THE DUTIES OF THE OFFICE OF MANAGEMENT AND
BUDGET AND THE DOMESTIC COUNCIL IN THE EXECUTIVE OFFICE
OF THE PRESIDENT
By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and 
statutes of the United States, including section 301 of title 3 of the 
United States Code, and pursuant to Reorganization Plan No. 2 of 
1970 (hereinafter referred to as “the Plan”) , it is ordered as follows :
S ection  1. (a) All functions transferred to the President of the 
United States by Part I  of the Plan (including the function vested by 
section 102(f) of designating the officials of the Office of Management 
and Budget who shall act as Director during the absence or disability of 
the Deputy Director or in the event of a vacancy in the office of Deputy 
Director) are hereby delegated to the Director of the Office of Man­
agement and Budget in the Executive Office of the President. Such 
functions shall be carried out by the Director under the direction of 
the President and pursuant to such further instructions as the 
President from time to time may issue.
(b) All outstanding delegations, rules, regulations, orders, circulars, 
bulletins, or other forms of Executive or administrative action issued 
or taken by or relating to the Bureau of the Budget or the Director 
of the Bureau of the Budget prior to the effective date of this order 
shall, until amended or revoked, remain in full force and effect as if 
issued or taken by or relating to the Office of Management and Budget 
or the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.
S ec. 2. (a) Under the direction of the President and subject to such 
further instructions as the President from time to time may issue, 
the Domestic Council in the Executive Office of the President shall (1) 
receive and develop information necessary for assessing national 
domestic needs and defining national domestic goals, and develop for 
the President alternative proposals for reaching those goals; (2) col­
laborate with the Office of Management and Budget and others in the 
determination of national domestic priorities for the allocation of 
available resources; (3) collaborate with the Office of Management and 
Budget and others to assure a continuing review of ongoing programs 
from the standpoint of their relative contributions to. national goals 
as compared-with their use of available resources; and (4) provide 
policy advice to the President on domestic issues.
(b) The organizations listed herein are terminated, and the func­
tions heretofore assigned to them shall be performed by the Domestic 
Council :
Council for Urban Affairs (Executive Order No. 11452 of Janu­
ary 23,1969)
Cabinet Committee on the Environment (Executive Order No. 
11472 of May 29,1969, as amended by Executive Order No. 11514 of 
March 5, 1970)
Council for Rural Affairs (Executive Order No. 11493 of Novem­
ber 13, 1969)
S ec. 3. This order shall be effective July 1,1970.
T he  W hite  H ouse,
J u ly 1,1970.
[F.R. Doc. 70-8544 ; Filed, July 1, 1970 ; 1:06 pm.]
FEDERAL REGISTER, V O L 35, NO. 128— THURSDAY, JULY 2, 1970

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
S ec. 2 . Functions of the Council.  The Council shall advise and as­
sist the President with respect to the further development-of the non­
metropolitan areas of the country and shall perform such other duties  
as the President may from time to time prescribe. In addition to such 
duties, the Council is directed to :
(1) Assist the President in the development of policies for rural  
areas, which shall include consideration of the affairs of the smaller  
cities and towns which lie outside the metropolitan areas.
(2) Secure information on the problems confronting rural America,  
identify their causes, and develop means to deal with them by using  
available programs or initiating new ones.
(3) Foster effective use and coordination of Federal programs in  
the non-metropolitan areas in order to improve the delivery of public  
services to the people.

By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Constitution and 
statutes of the United States, including section 301 of title 3 of the 
United States Code, and pursuant to Reorganization Plan No. 2 of

Director) are hereby delegated to the Director of the Office of Man­
agement and Budget in the Executive Office of the President. Such

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11493
ESTABLISHING THE COUNCIL FOR RURAL AFFAIRS
W HEREAS rural America is vitally important to this Nation’s  
total economy and society ;  and
W HEREAS there is a need to provide expanded employment op­
portunities and more attractive living conditions outside the metro­
politan areas; and
W HEREAS a viable rural America would offer an opportunity for  
farmers and other rural residents to share in the economic, growth of  
the country:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
the Constitution and statutes of the United States, and as President  
of the United States, it is ordered as follows:
S ection  1. Establishment of the Council,  (a) There is hereby es­
tablished the Council for Rural Affairs (hereinafter referred to as  
“the Council”).
(b) The President of the United States shall preside over meetings  
of the Council. The Vice President shall preside in the absence of the  
President.
(c) The Council shall be composed of the following:
The Vice President of the United States
Secretary of Agriculture
Secretary of Interior
Secretary of Commerce
Secretary of Health, Education and Welfare
Secretary of Housing and Urban Development
Secretary of Labor
Chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers  
Director of the Bureau of the Budget  
Director of the Office of Economic Opportunity
and such other heads of departments and agencies as the President may  
from time to time direct.
S ec. 2 . Functions of the Council.  The Council shall advise and as­
sist the President with respect to the further development-of the non­
metropolitan areas of the country and shall perform such other duties  
as the President may from time to time prescribe. In addition to such 
duties, the Council is directed to :
(1) Assist the President in the development of policies for rural  
areas, which shall include consideration of the affairs of the smaller  
cities and towns which lie outside the metropolitan areas.
(2) Secure information on the problems confronting rural America,  
identify their causes, and develop means to deal with them by using  
available programs or initiating new ones.
(3) Foster effective use and coordination of Federal programs in  
the non-metropolitan areas in order to improve the delivery of public  
services to the people.

rural areas are taken into account.

research_rationale: EO 11493 (signed 1969-11-13, 34 FR 18289-18290), read in full from the held official FR text: secs. 1-4 establishing the Council for Rural Affairs. The dossier's clause inventory omits sec. 1(a) and merges duty (7) with sec. 3, so a corrected inventory of seven disjoint spans (enacting words through sec. 4, skipping only the FR page footer and header between duties (3) and (4)) replaces it. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:11493>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own. The by-number scan finds 11493 only in EO 11541 and EO 12553 (the EO 9370 hit is an Alien Property page number); 'Council for Rural Affairs' appears only in EO 11493, EO 11541 and EO 12553; the OFR catalog records the EO 11541 termination ('affects the council', 1970-07-01) and the EO 12553 revocation. No held order amended EO 11493 between 1969-11-13 and 1970-07-01. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is therefore only an upper bound: the first end is EO 11541 on 1970-07-01 (its provision is cited from the held actor text because the scanner did not locate it), and EO 12553 is attached as a later event. First end: EO 11541, 1970-07-01. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 11541 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11541.txt, 35 FR 10737, read in full): sec. 2(b) terminates the Council for Rural Affairs and provides that 'the functions heretofore assigned to them shall be performed by the Domestic Council'; sec. 3 makes the order effective July 1, 1970. Own-residual check, reading EO 11493 in full: it established an advisory council with advisory and coordinating duties and created no fund, property or private right. Its functions were carried forward by EO 11541 to the Domestic Council (a successor provision of EO 11541, not a continuation of EO 11493), so the clauses end and their subject is transferred: transferred_or_accrued. Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, text_sha256 6361bdc5..., 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15, read for this purpose: heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966 and the signature block): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording anywhere in the held text (searched saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that). EO 12553 adds no savings for the already-terminated order. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); a subject-word scan of the same texts; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
of the United States Code and in conformity with the first section of 
the Act of February 19, 1966 (80 Stat. 5; Public Law 89-355), I  
hereby designate the Department of Commerce as the Department 
through which the United States shall, under that Act, participate in 
the Inter-American Cultural and Trade Center (Interama) in Dade 
County, Florida. In  carrying out that function, the Department is 
authorized to exercise the authority vested in me by the first section 
of the Act of February 19,1966.

THE PRESIDENT 8279
Executive Order 11286
DESIGNATING THE DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE AS THE DEPARTMENT  
THROUGH WHICH THE UNITED STATES SHALL PARTICIPATE IN THE  
INTER-AMERICAN CULTURAL AND TRADE CENTER IN DADE COUNTY,  
FLORIDA
By virtue of the authority vested in me by Section 301 of Title 3 
of the United States Code and in conformity with the first section of 
the Act of February 19, 1966 (80 Stat. 5; Public Law 89-355), I  
hereby designate the Department of Commerce as the Department 
through which the United States shall, under that Act, participate in 
the Inter-American Cultural and Trade Center (Interama) in Dade 
County, Florida. In  carrying out that function, the Department is 
authorized to exercise the authority vested in me by the first section 
of the Act of February 19,1966.
L yndon  B. J ohnson
T h e W h ite H ouse,
Ju ne 10,1966.
[F.R. Doc. 66-6539; Filed, June 10, 1966; 3:04 pan.]
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 31, NO. 114— TUESDAY, JUNE 14, 1966

research_rationale: EO 11286 (signed 1966-06-10, 31 FR 8279), read in full from the held official FR text: one sentence designating the Department of Commerce for United States participation in Interama under Pub. L. 89-355. The dossier's single clause covers the whole operative text. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:11286>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order has no sunset, term, condition or termination clause of its own: it is one designation sentence with no period. The by-number scan finds 11286 only in EO 12553 (the EO 10302 hit is an FR page number in a contents list); 'Interama' and 'Inter-American Cultural and Trade Center' appear in no other held order text; the OFR catalog records only the EO 12553 revocation. Non-express lead only, not an end: whether the Act of February 19, 1966 (Pub. L. 89-355) was later repealed or its federal participation wound up before 1986 was not established (statute history not held; no held instrument or OFR note says any statute acted on EO 11286). The order is therefore recorded as ending at its first express end, EO 12553, which the President described as eliminating orders 'no longer necessary'; this is not proof of continuous operation to 1986. First end: EO 12553, 1986-02-25. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive Order 11307
COORDINATION OF FEDERAL PROGRAMS AFFECTING AGRICULTURAL  
AND RURAL AREA DEVELOPMENT
W H E R E AS the development of our Nation’s agricultural and 
rural areas has undergone radical changes due to technological ad­
vancement and the increasing urbanization of the Nation’s society and 
economy ; and
W H E R E AS the living standards and welfare of the rural area 
population depend upon a successf ul accommodation to these changes ; 
and
W H E R E AS Congress has vested responsibilities in the Secretary of 
Agriculture for the administration of numerous programs aimed at the 
achievement of sound agricultural and rural development; and
W H E R E AS such programs are closely interrelated with important 
programs and activities administered by other Federal departments 
and agencies, which affect agricultural and rural area development; 
and
W H E R E AS the President has directed the Secretary of Agriculture 
to put the facilities of Department of Agriculture field offices at the 
disposal of all Federal agencies to assist them in making their pro­
grams effective in rural areas, and jointly with the Director of the 
Bureau of the Budget to review with the head of each department or 
agency the administrative obstacles which may stand in the way of 
equitable distribution in rural areas of the benefits of their programs 
and to propose administrative or legislative steps which can be taken 
to assure that equity is attained to assure full participation by rural 
areas ; and
W H E R E AS the highest level of coordination is required between 
the Department of Agriculture and such other Federal departments 
and agencies in order to achieve the maximum beneficial impact on 
agricultural and rural area development :
— NOW, TH EREFO RE, by virtue of the authority vested in me as 
President of the United States, it is ordered as follows :
S ectio n  1. Responsibilities of the Secretary, (a) The Secretary 
of Agriculture, shall take the initiative in identifying problems of 
agricultural and rural area development which require the coopera­
tion of various Federal departments and agencies for their effective 
solution, and pursuant thereto shall convene, or authorize his repre­
sentatives to convene, meetings at appropriate times and places, to 
which he shall invite the heads of such departments and agencies as 
may be responsible for interrelated programs or activities, or repre­
sentatives designated by them, for the following purposes : __
(1) To provide a forum for consideration of mutual problems con­
cerning Federal programs and activities affecting agricultural and 
rural area development and for the exchange of information needed 
to achieve coordination of, and to avoid duplication in, such programs 
and activities.
(2) To promote cooperation among Federal departments and agen­
cies in achieving consistent policies, practices, and procedures for 
administration of their programs affecting agricultural and rural area 
development.
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 31, NO. 192— TUESDAY, OCTOBER 4, 1966

(3) To consult with and obtain the advice of appropriate Federal 
departments and agencies with respect to :
(A ) intergovernmental relations and cooperation in promoting 
sound agricultural and rural area development ;
(B ) provision of information and technical assistance to State and 
local governments in solving agricultural and rural area development 
problems; and
(C ) encouragement of comprehensive planning of, and effective 
regional, State, and local cooperation in agricultural and rural area 
development activities.
(4) To identify agricultural and rural area development problems 
of particular States, regions, or localities which require interagency or 
intergovernmental coordination.
(b ) The Secretary shall make arrangements with such Federal 
departments and agencies for such working groups as they shall agree 
may be desirable to consider special problems arising with respect to 
matters described in subsection (a) oi this section.
S ec . 2. Agency responsibilities. The heads of Federal depart­
ments and agencies having programs which have an impact on agri­
cultural or rural area development shall to the extent permitted by 
law and funds available, furnish information, at the request of the 
Secretary, pertaining to programs within the responsibilities of such 
departments or agencies, and such additional information as will assist 
the Secretary in developing solutions to agricultural and rural area 
development problems.

research_rationale: EO 11307 (signed 1966-09-30, 31 FR 12917-12918), read in full from the held official FR text: enacting words and secs. 1-5 on coordination of Federal programs affecting agricultural and rural area development. The dossier's clause inventory omits the enacting words and sec. 1(a) lead-in and merges secs. 1(b)-4(a) and 4(b)-5, so a corrected inventory of eleven disjoint spans (enacting words through sec. 5, skipping only the FR page footer and header between items (2) and (3)) replaces it. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:11307>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order has no sunset, term, condition or termination clause of its own; sec. 5 (superseding EO 11122) is an act by this order on another order, not an end of this order. The by-number scan finds 11307 only in EO 12553 (the EO 11321 hit is inside an FR page-citation list and the EO 11671 hit is its own FR page, 37 FR 11307); the OFR catalog records EO 11307 superseding EO 11122 (as actor) and only the EO 12553 revocation as acting on it. The order is therefore recorded as ending at its first express end, EO 12553, which the President described as eliminating orders 'no longer necessary'; this is not proof of continuous operation to 1986. W H E R E A S  Federal legislation enacted in recent years has estab­
lished numerous manpower program s to im prove the em ployability

ernments and nongovernment agencies; and

section 637 o f the Econom ic O pportunity A c t o f 1964, as amended 
(4 2  U .S .C . 2 9 7 9 ), and as President o f the U nited States, it is ordered

power training and supportive manpower service program s is hereby

manpower training or supportive manpower service program s sh all,

Com m erce; H ousing and U rban D evelopm ent; A g ricu ltu re ; and the 
In te rio r; the Office o f Econom ic O p p ortu n ity; and the C ivil Service 
Com m ission, together w ith their affiliated organizations and such addi­
tional Federal executive departm ents and agencies as m ay be m utually 
agreed upon by them , shall participate in C A M P S  fo r the purposes o f 
cooperatively planning and executing m anpower program s and sup­
portive m anpower service program s in urban and rural areas.

research_rationale: EO 11422 (signed 1968-08-15, 33 FR 11739-11740), read in full from the held official FR text: recitals, enacting words and secs. 1-4 on the Cooperative Area Manpower Planning System. The dossier's 9 clauses cover the whole operative text with no gap. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:11422>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order has no sunset, term, condition or termination clause of its own. The by-number scan finds 11422 in EO 12107 (sec. 2-101(b) list of amended orders, read in context) and EO 12553; the EO 9912 and EO 9913 hits are FR document numbers (47-11422). The OFR catalog records the EO 12107 amendment and the EO 12553 revocation. EO 12107 (effective 1979-01-01) substituted 'Office of Personnel Management' for 'Civil Service Commission' in sec. 2(b): an amendment, attached as a later event on that clause, not an end (the dossier's gap 'target provision not located: EO:12107' is closed by citing the held EO 12107 actor text). Non-express lead only, not an end: the manpower programs CAMPS coordinated are believed to have been overtaken by the Comprehensive Employment and Training Act of 1973 (statute not held; it names no executive order and no held instrument or OFR note says it acted on EO 11422). The order is therefore recorded as ending at its first express end, EO 12553, which the President described as eliminating orders 'no longer necessary'; this is not proof of continuous operation to 1986. First end: EO 12553, 1986-02-25. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, text_sha256 6361bdc5..., 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15, read for this purpose: heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966 and the signature block): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording anywhere in the held text (searched saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that). Own-residual check, reading EO 11422 in full: it stated a coordination policy and recognized an interagency planning system with committees and Labor Department staff support; it created no fund, property or private right, and its plans and committee work were completed administrative acts; grants and contracts of participating agencies rested on their own statutes. EO 12107's sec. 2-403 transfers concern Civil Service Commission functions, not EO 11422. EO 12553 has no savings clause. Nothing of the order outlives its revocation. research_rationale: EO 12129 (signed 1979-04-05, 44 FR 21001-21002), read in full from the held official FR text: enacting words and secs. 1-101 to 1-110 establishing the Critical Energy Facility Program. The OCR text layer of the enacting words and secs. 1-101 to 1-102 is badly garbled (official PDF pages not inspected; original_pages_confirmed false). The dossier's clause inventory omits the enacting words, secs. 1-101, 1-102 and the sec. 1-103 lead-in and merges sec. 1-104(e)-(f) with secs. 1-105 to 1-110(a), so a corrected inventory of nine disjoint spans (enacting words through sec. 1-110, skipping only the page break between secs. 1-104 and 1-105) replaces it. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:12129>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order has no sunset, term, condition or termination clause of its own and no effective-date wording; the deadlines in secs. 1-102, 1-104, 1-105 and 1-108 are permit-decision schedules and reporting, not an end of any clause, and no report deadline is relied on. The by-number scan finds 12129 only in EO 12553 (the EO 12593 hits are FR page-range and CFR parts-affected index entries); 'Critical Energy Facility' appears in no other held order text; the OFR catalog and jobs/status-history record only the EO 12553 revocation; the U.S. Code machine hits are the 42 U.S.C. 2235 editorial note, which says EO 12129 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986'. No amendment, extension or suspension of EO 12129 is held. No non-express statutory or decontrol lead was identified: the Program is an OMB coordination scheme resting on general Presidential authority, not on a temporary statute. The order is therefore recorded as ending at its first express end, EO 12553, which the President described as eliminating orders 'no longer necessary'; this is not proof of continuous operation to 1986. First end: EO 12553, 1986-02-25. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, text_sha256 6361bdc5..., 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15, read for this purpose: heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966 and the signature block): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording anywhere in the held text (searched saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that). Own-residual check, reading EO 12129 in full: it set up an OMB-run coordination program with agency data submissions, deadline schedules and interagency review mechanisms; it created no fund, property or private right, and sec. 1-110 expressly left statutory review duties and State, local and public participation unchanged, so every permit decision rested on the agencies' own statutes. Its schedules and coordination were completed administrative acts. EO 12553 has no savings clause. Nothing of the order outlives its revocation. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); a subject-word scan of the same texts; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

the United States of America, including Section 126a(2) of the Atomic Energy

research_rationale: EO 12193 (signed 1980-02-12, 45 FR 9885), read in full from the held official FR text: one sentence making a sec. 126a(2) determination and extending the period to March 10, 1981. The dossier's machine inventory (scopes #lead, #1980, #1, #2, #3, #4, #1980-dup2) starts mid-sentence at 'I hereby extend' and otherwise takes in the editorial note, a blank page and the neighbouring Rules and Regulations documents on PDF pages 10-11, which are not part of EO 12193; a corrected inventory of one span (enacting and determination words through 'March 10,1981.', offsets 731-1471) replaces it. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:12193>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order's only operative content is an extension of a statutory period to a fixed date, March 10, 1981; that is a fixed date, not a report deadline. Held orders naming 12193 are EO 12295, EO 12553 and later EURATOM extension orders (EO 12351, 12409, 12463, 12506, 12554, 12587, 12629, 12670, 12706, 12753, 12791, 12840, 12903, 12955), each read in the relevant part: they recite EO 12193 in the list of orders that extended the period and then extend it again by their own determination; none amends, suspends or revives EO 12193. EO 12295 (signed 1981-02-24, before the 1981-03-10 expiry) extends the period from March 10, 1981 to March 10, 1982 by its own determination; it does not say it amends or supersedes EO 12193, so EO 12193's extension ran its full term and EO 12295's took over at its end. The dossier's machine 'supersede' chain records from EO 12629, 12706, 12791, 12840, 12903 and 12955 are misattributions: each of those orders supersedes only its immediate predecessor, not EO 12193, and all are after 1986. The dossier gaps 'target provision not located' for EO 12295, 12351, 12506, 12554 and 12753 are OFR 'See' cross-references (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv kind cross_reference), not events: their held texts contain no provision acting on EO 12193, only recitals, so they are closed as recitals, not left as material gaps. EO 12554 (1986-02-28) still recites EO 12193 three days after its revocation, which confirms the recital is history, not continuation. The EO 12593 hit is an index number and the EO 9920 hit is a file SHA-256 string. EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is therefore only an upper bound: the first end is the 1981-03-10 expiry, and EO 12553 is attached as a later event. Whether a recital in a later extension keeps an expired extension order alive is not asserted by any held source; the producer reads the recitals as history. Nothing relies on the pending report-deadline or transcription-as-copy rulings. First end: EO 12193, 1981-03-10. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 12553 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt, text_sha256 6361bdc5..., 51 FR 7237, PDF pages 9-15, read for this purpose: heading, the single operative sentence at offsets 691-966 and the signature block): 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked:' followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; no exception, savings, pending-matter, transfer or 'nothing herein' wording anywhere in the held text (searched saving, nothing in, shall not affect, pending, heretofore, notwithstanding, provided that). Own-residual check, reading EO 12193 in full: it made one determination and extended a statutory period to 1981-03-10; cooperation with EURATOM during that year was a completed matter, and every later year rests on its own extension order. It created no office, fund, property or private right. EO 12553 has no savings clause. Nothing of the order outlived 1981-03-10. Bounded search: the order and EO 12553 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); a subject-word scan of the same texts; the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

research_rationale: EO 12415 (signed 1983-04-05, 48 FR 15117), read in full from the held official FR text: one sentence amending Sec. 4(b) of EO 12358 to set the Commission's termination on December 31, 1983. The dossier's single clause (#whole, 'By the authority vested' through the closing quotation mark) is the whole operative text; the editorial note and the neighbouring Rules and Regulations pages are outside it. Inventory confirmed without correction. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; the record ACT:EO:12415>EO:12553 is an agent-located Rastell record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step; simulated ingestion, not yet in the committed build) revokes it by number. D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 12553, or the order's own dated term, end the order or a clause before 1986-02-25?): The order's own words fix the Commission's termination on December 31, 1983; that is a termination date, not a report deadline (neither EO 12415 nor EO 12358 contains any reporting requirement). The by-number scan finds 12415 only in EO 12553 (the EO 14257 hit is a tariff heading number). EO 12376 (1982) amended EO 12358's membership sentence and does not touch Sec. 4(b); no held order after EO 12415 amends Sec. 4(b) again or extends the Commission. EO 12415's end rests on its own words, not on a whole-text restatement or on an event that does not name it, so the open owner method question raised in the probe does not arise here (it does arise for EO 12376, which is blocked). EO 12553 (1986-02-25) is therefore only an upper bound: the first end is 1983-12-31, and EO 12553 is attached as a later event. Same pattern as the probe's EO 12269 and EO 12351 (own dated term). operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: Directs the Civil Service Commission to refuse examination or certification to any person employed in the civilian executive branch within three months unless the employing office assents; own term 'until the Congress or the President declares that the present emergency has ceased to exist'. Ended with the whole order: EO 9830 Part III revokes it by number, effective 1947-05-01 under EO 9830's enacting clause. The order's own term ('This order shall continue in effect until the Congress or the President declares that the present emergency has ceased to exist') did not run before 1947-05-01: no held instrument declares the emergency (Proclamation 2487 of the same day, May 27, 1941, and the 1939 emergency) ended before then; the cessation-of-hostilities proclamation of December 31, 1946 is not such a declaration, and the national emergencies were terminated only in 1952. EO 9063 (February 16, 1942, held, read) authorized the Commission to adopt special wartime procedures (the War Service Regulations) but neither revokes, suspends nor names EO 8760; the President still listed EO 8760 among the orders to be revoked in 1947. No amendment, extension, suspension or earlier partial end of this clause by any other instrument was found before 1947-05-01 (D6), so no later event is attached.

CHAPTER V III— SUGAR DIVISION OF 
THE AGRICULTURAL ADJUST­
MENT ADM INISTRATION
P art 802—S ugar  D eterm inations
DETERMINATION OF FARMING PRACTICES TO BE 
CARRIED OUT IN CONNECTION WITH THE  
PRODUCTION OF THE 1941 CROP OF SUGAR­
CANE IN THE MAINLAND CANE SUGAR AREA
Pursuant to the provisions of section 
301 (e) of the Sugar Act of 1937, as 
amended, I, Paul H. Appleby, Under Sec­
retary of Agriculture, do hereby make 
the following determination:
§ 802.23c Farming practices in con­
nection with the production of the 1941  
crop of sugarcane in the mainland cane  
sugar area — (a) Soil-building require­
ment.  The conditions prescribed in sub­
section (e) of section 301 of the Sugar 
Act of 1937, as amended, shall be deemed 
to have been fulfilled with respect to the 
production of the 1941 crop of sugarcane 
for sugar on any farm in the mainland 
cane sugar area if there is carried out 
in 1941, on land on the farm which is 
adapted to the production of sugarcane 
for sugar, an acreage of soil-building 
practices equal to not less than 30 per
centum of the acreage of sugarcane for 
sugar growing on the farm for harvest 
in 1941.
(b) Approved practices.  (1) Each 
acre of the following shall be counted as 
one acre of soil-building practices:
(1) Seeding winter legumes.
(ii) Plowing or disking under a good 
stand and good growth of a green 
manure crop, or cover crop (excluding 
lespedeza, peanuts hogged off, and non- 
leguminous cover crops).
(iii) Turning under a good stand and 
good growth of summer legumes (exclud­
ing peanuts, lespedeza, and summer leg­
umes used as truck crops) NOT inter- 
planted or grown in combination with 
row crops such as corn.
(2) Each two acres of the following 
shall be counted as one acre of soil­
building practices:
(i) Turning under a good stand and 
good growth of summer legumes (exclud­
ing peanuts, lespedeza, and summer leg­
umes used as truck crops) interplanted 
or grown in combination with row crops, 
such as corn, provided the summer leg­
ume occupies at least one-third of the 
land.
(3) Each of the following practices in 
the amounts specified shall be counted as 
one acre of soil-building practices if ap­
plied to a full seeding of winter legumes.
(i) Application of 300 pounds of 16- 
percent superphosphate (or its equiva­
lent) to, or in connection with the seed­
ing of, winter legumes.
(ii) Application of 500 pounds of basic 
slag or rock phosphate (including Col­
loidal phosphate) to, or in connection 
with the seeding of, winter legumes.
(4) Each one and one-half acres of 
land the top soil of which is combustible 
(determined as such by the State Agri­
cultural Conservation Committee) on 
which there are carried out the practices 
specified in paragraphs B, C, D, and E 
of Amendment 3 to Southern Region 
Bulletin 101, issued June 11, 1937, for 
protecting the soil against fire, assuring 
adequate drainage, and preventing soil 
oxidation and subsidence, shall be 
counted as one acre of soil-building prac­
tices: Provided, however,  That there shall 
be carried out on such land on the farm 
such other practices as are recommended 
for the farm by the County Agricultural 
Conservation Committee, and approved 
by the State Agricultural Conservation 
Committee, for protecting the soil against 
fire, assuring adequate drainage, prevent­
ing soil oxidation and subsidence, and 
otherwise preserving and improving the 
fertility of the soil and preventing soil 
erosion, such practices to be consistent 
with reasonable standards of the farm­
ing community in which the land is 
located.
(c) Standards of performance.  Hie 
soil conserving practices shall be carried 
out on the farm in accordance with 
farming methods commonly used in the 
community in which the farm is located

research_rationale: EO 8760 (signed 1941-05-27, 6 FR 2618), read in full from the held official FR text: one operative paragraph (restriction on examination and certification of federal employees without the employing office's written assent) and an own term tied to a declaration that the emergency has ceased. It is revoked by number in EO 9830 Part III, effective 1947-05-01 (the enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947' governs Part III; signing and FR filing on 1947-02-24 are not the effective date). The ACT record ACT:EO:8760>EO:9830 is an agent-located record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step (simulated ingestion; not yet in the committed build). D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 9830 end the order or a clause before 1947-05-01?): The order's own term ('This order shall continue in effect until the Congress or the President declares that the present emergency has ceased to exist') did not run before 1947-05-01: no held instrument declares the emergency (Proclamation 2487 of the same day, May 27, 1941, and the 1939 emergency) ended before then; the cessation-of-hostilities proclamation of December 31, 1946 is not such a declaration, and the national emergencies were terminated only in 1952. EO 9063 (February 16, 1942, held, read) authorized the Commission to adopt special wartime procedures (the War Service Regulations) but neither revokes, suspends nor names EO 8760; the President still listed EO 8760 among the orders to be revoked in 1947. The by-number scan finds 8760 only in EO 9830 (plus page numbers in EO 11906 and EO 8193A); the OFR catalog records only the EO 9830 revocation; no held order 1941-1947 repeats or changes the written-assent rule (search for 'refuse exam' and 'written assent' finds only EO 8760). No earlier end of the order or of any clause was found, so every clause is terminated on 1947-05-01 and no later event is attached. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

Own-residual check, reading EO 8760 in full: it governed admission to examinations and certification of serving federal employees; it created no office, fund, property or private right, and EO 9830 contains no comparable assent rule (searched 'assent', 'three months'). Assents given and examinations refused before 1947-05-01 were completed administrative acts with no continuing force from the order. EO 9830 has no savings clause reaching it. Nothing of the order outlives its revocation. By virtue of the authority vested in 
•me by section 1753 of the Revised Stat­
utes and by the Civil Service Act (22 
Stat. 403), it is hereby ordered as follows: 
When a disabled veteran shall have 
completed a course of training prescribed 
by the Administrator of Veterans’  Af­
fairs in accordance with the provisions 
of the act of March 24,1943, Public Law 
16, 78th Congress, in any department, 
independent establishment, or agency of 
the Executive branch of the Federal 
Government, such veteran may be ap­
pointed to the position for which the 
training was received without regard to 
the requirements of the Civil Service 
Rules and the War Service Regulations: 
Provided, that the veteran is recom­
mended for such appointment by the 
employing agency, that the Civil Service 
Commission determines that the course 
of training is adequate for the satisfac­
tory performance of the duties of the po­
sition, and that the veteran passes, prior 
to appointment, such noncompetitive 
examination as the Commission may 
prescribe.

Own-residual check, reading EO 9503 in full: appointments of disabled veterans made under it before 1947-05-01 are completed acts. EO 9830 Part I itself carries the subject forward as its own new rule: Rule III lists among persons who may be given competitive status '(3) Any disabled veteran who, in a manner satisfactory to the Commission, has completed a course of training in the executive branch of the Government prescribed by the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs in accordance with the act of March 24, 1943 (57 Stat. 43)' (EO 9830 text offset 27625). That is a successor provision of EO 9830, not a continuation of EO 9503, so the clause ends but its subject is carried forward and its completed appointments stand: transferred_or_accrued. EO 9830 has no savings clause reaching it. research_rationale: EO 9668 (signed 1945-12-28, 11 FR 4), read in full from the held official FR text: one sentence rewriting paragraph 6 of Subdivision III of Schedule A. It is revoked by number in EO 9830 Part III, effective 1947-05-01 (the enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947' governs Part III; signing and FR filing on 1947-02-24 are not the effective date). The ACT record ACT:EO:9668>EO:9830 is an agent-located record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step (simulated ingestion; not yet in the committed build). D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 9830 end the order or a clause before 1947-05-01?): The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own. The by-number scan finds 9668 only in EO 9830 (plus a page number in EO 9773 and the neighbouring orders 9666-9670 on the same pages, where EO 9669 merely says 'see Executive Order 9668, supra'); the OFR catalog records only the EO 9830 revocation (its two order-text edges on EO 9668 are OCR artefacts 'EO:9' from the neighbouring EO 9667). Paragraph 6 of Subdivision III was not changed again before EO 9830 (held orders mentioning 'insolvent national' 1945-1947: EO 9666-9670 on the same pages, EO 9830, and EO 9848, which is later). No earlier end of the order or of any clause was found, so every clause is terminated on 1947-05-01 and no later event is attached. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 9830 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9830.txt, text_sha256 b519c570..., 12 FR 1259 ff., read for this purpose: enacting clause, Parts I-III and every revocation row): the enacting clause 'it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:' (offsets 2164-2220) governs Parts I (Civil Service Rules), II (Schedules) and III; Part III (from offset 90277) is the single sentence 'The following Executive orders are hereby revoked:' followed by a one-per-line list of orders, with no exception, savings, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording; a search of the whole text for 'shall not affect', 'heretofore', 'pending', 'nothing herein', 'remain in effect', 'continue in effect' and 'supersed' finds no savings clause for revoked orders (the only 'heretofore' hit, at 30777, concerns persons appointed under the new Rule III sec. 3.2). Own-residual check, reading EO 9668 in full: appointments of receivers and their employees made before 1947-05-01 are completed acts. EO 9830 Part II re-lists receivers in its own Schedule A in narrower words: 'Treasury ... (vi) Receivers of insolvent national banks and other financial institutions which are filled by appointment by the Comptroller of the Currency and whose salaries are paid directly from the funds of insolvent institutions' (EO 9830 text offset 46656), without 'and the employees of such receivers'. That is re-enactment by the successor order, not continuation of EO 9668: the clause ends, the receiver exception is carried forward, the employees' exception is not. transferred_or_accrued. EO 9830 has no savings clause reaching it. Bounded search: the order and EO 9830 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts; every hit read in context); the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv); a check of catalog titles of unheld orders between the order and EO 9830 for any personnel-rule change; the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

It is revoked by number in EO 9830 Part III, effective 1947-05-01 (the enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947' governs Part III; signing and FR filing on 1947-02-24 are not the effective date). The ACT record ACT:EO:8423>EO:9830 is an agent-located record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step (simulated ingestion; not yet in the committed build). D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 9830 end the order or a clause before 1947-05-01?): The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own; the words 'positions in Federal agencies concerned in preparedness and the national defense program' limit the objection grounds, not the life of the order. The by-number scan of held FR order texts 1940-1947 finds 8423 only in EO 9830 (its Part III row and the codification table) and in the FR pages shared with EO 8424/8425; the other hits are commodity table numbers in EO 8702/8703. Every held 1940-1947 'Rule VII' hit was read: EO 8424/8425 (same FR issue), and EO 9428 (1944-02-29), which only refers to Rule VII when granting status to certain fingerprint classifiers and does not amend sec. 2(b). 'Highest three' hits: EO 8576 (separate regulations for unclassified positions) and the War Service Regulations sec. 18.4(c) as amended (held in EO_9524.txt), a parallel selection rule for war-service appointments under EO 9063 that neither names nor amends Rule VII sec. 2(b) (scope lead, not an end). EO 9691 (1946-02-04, held, read) directs that within thirty days all classified-service actions 'shall be made in accordance with the Civil Service Rules and Regulations', which presupposes Rule VII as amended remained in force. No earlier end of the order or of any clause was found, so every clause is terminated on 1947-05-01 and no later event is attached. Savings: none_after_bounded_search (see savings_residuals). research_rationale: EO 8894 (signed 1941-09-08, 6 FR 4681-4682, FR issue of 1941-09-12), read in full from the held official FR text: enacting words and a rewrite of Civil Service Rule II sec. 6, printed across a page break, with a corrected inventory of two spans. It is revoked by number in EO 9830 Part III, effective 1947-05-01 (the enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947' governs Part III; signing and FR filing on 1947-02-24 are not the effective date). The ACT record ACT:EO:8894>EO:9830 is an agent-located record upheld by an independent AI reviewer with a D6 step (simulated ingestion; not yet in the committed build). D6 / earlier-end test (did any instrument other than EO 9830 end the order or a clause before 1947-05-01?): The order has no sunset, term or termination clause of its own. The time conditions in the text (six months' service, sixty days thereafter, recommendation within one year of reinstatement) are eligibility conditions for status, not ends of the order or report deadlines, so neither pending ruling is relied on. The by-number scan of held FR order texts 8895-9860 finds no citation of 8894 other than EO 9830's Part III row; the OFR catalog records only the EO 9830 revocation. Every held 1941-1947 'Rule II' hit was read: EO 9230 (Board of Legal Examiners, 1942) twice applies 'Section 6 of Civil Service Rule II' to attorney positions (status after six months on compliance with sec. 6; noncompetitive examination prescribed with the Board's approval). That applies the rule as it stood and neither amends nor suspends it. No held instrument amends 'section 6 of Civil Service Rule II' after 1941-09-08 (the phrase occurs only in EO 8894 and EO 9230). EO 9063 and the War Service Regulations created a separate war-service route without naming Rule II sec. 6. EO 9830 itself replaces the subject with new sec. 3.1(b)(1) (offset 26565 ff.), which shows the rule was still treated as live in 1947. No earlier end of the order or of any clause was found, so every clause is terminated on 1947-05-01 and no later event is attached. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (see savings_residuals). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification and not a status.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record for EO 9830 (held FR text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9830.txt, text_sha256 b519c570..., 12 FR 1259 ff., read for this purpose: enacting clause, Parts I-III and every revocation row): the enacting clause 'it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:' (offsets 2164-2220) governs Parts I (Civil Service Rules), II (Schedules) and III; Part III (from offset 90277) is the single sentence 'The following Executive orders are hereby revoked:' followed by a one-per-line list of orders, with no exception, savings, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording; a search of the whole text for 'shall not affect', 'heretofore', 'pending', 'nothing herein', 'remain in effect', 'continue in effect' and 'supersed' finds no savings clause for revoked orders (the only 'heretofore' hit, at 30777, concerns persons appointed under the new Rule III sec. 3.2). Own-residual check, reading EO 8894 in full: classified status conferred under new Rule II sec. 6 before 1947-05-01 is a completed act and stands. The subject is carried forward by the successor order, not by EO 8894: EO 9830 sec. 3.1 (offset 26565) provides that 'the following classes of persons may acquire a competitive status: (1) Any person holding a permanent position when it is placed in the competitive service by statute or Executive order or is otherwise made subject to competitive examination', under such noncompetitive examination, time limits or other requirements as the Commission may prescribe. That is re-enactment in different terms by the successor order on the same date, not continuation of EO 8894. transferred_or_accrued. EO 9830 has no savings clause reaching it. Bounded search: the order and EO 9830 read in full in the held official FR texts; a by-number scan of the held FR order texts (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts, EO 8706-9860 and every hit read in context); the OFR catalog edges for the order (jobs/later-events EDGES.csv: only 'Revoked by: EO 9830, February 24, 1947'); a check of the catalog titles of the 76 unheld orders between EO 8894 and EO 9830 for any Civil Service Rule or Schedule change (none: only individual appointments without regard to the Rules, an Alien Property Division appointment authority and Coast and Geodetic Survey personnel transfers); the three machine searches (OFR catalog, U.S. Code, eCFR) read with their scope notes.

research_rationale: EO 10587 (signed 1955-01-13, 20 FR 361; Trading with the Enemy Act sec. 32(h)), read in full from the held FR text, has three operative sections (designation of the Jewish Restitution Successor Organization, delegation to the Attorney General, power to subdelegate) and no term or sunset. The dossier inventory omitted sec. 1, so the inventory is corrected by overrides to secs. 1-3. EO 11086 (1963-02-26, 28 FR 1833, held official text) restated all three sections: sec. 1 in substance unchanged (a partial amendment, attached), secs. 2 and 3 replaced by different texts, so the original words of secs. 2 and 3 ended on 1963-02-26. The order as amended ran until EO 12553 revoked it: EO 12553 revokes EO 10587 'and any amendments thereto' and also lists EO 11086 in its own row. EO 12553 (51 FR 7237, signed February 25, 1986; held official FR text, text sha256 6361bdc5...) says 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked' and lists the order in its 'No. Subject' table; it has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is READ as effective on signing, the on_signing reading 1986-02-25 (FR publication 1986-03-03 is not an effective date); this date is an upper bound, not a certified end. Sec. 1 is the last clause to end, so the whole-order end is the on_signing reading 1986-02-25. EO 11086 is not the whole-order end because it left sec. 1 in force. Earlier-end test: the OFR catalog, U.S. Code and eCFR searches show only EO 11086 and EO 12553; a number search of the held fr-originals texts finds no other order naming EO 10587. Statutory leads (Pub. L. 87-846 sec. 204(a) rewrote sec. 32(h); the programme's later lapse) are not held as text, are not express ends of this order's sec. 1 and are recorded only as context. No report deadline or other unheld date is needed for any clause's first end here; the discharge-conditioned text of restated sec. 3 belongs to EO 11086.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12553 (EO 12553, 51 FR 7237, read once in full): one operative sentence revoking the listed orders 'and any amendments thereto', no savings, continuation, transfer, exception or delayed-effect wording, so EO 12553 saves and transfers nothing. Own-residual check, reading EO 10587 and EO 11086 in full: EO 10587 designated the Jewish Restitution Successor Organization as successor in interest under sec. 32(h) of the Trading with the Enemy Act and delegated the President's sec. 32(h) functions (first to the Attorney General, from 1963 to the Foreign Claims Settlement Commission, with the Attorney General keeping jurisdiction over claims filed before the 1962 amendment). A completed designation, claims filed by the organization and payments or discharges made under the delegated functions are accrued effects that rest on the statute and on completed acts, not on the revoked order, and nothing in EO 12553 undoes them. operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (1961-01-17, effective on filing for publication, 1961-01-18; 26 FR 508): returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by the listed chapters of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 'shall be open to inspection by certain classes of persons and State and Federal Government establishments' under the Treasury decision approved the same day; the last paragraph supersedes EO 10738 of 1957-11-15 to the extent it applied to inspection by State tax officials of estate and gift-tax returns. The dossier splits this text into a clause and a fragment ('1954.'); the override restates it as one clause covering both paragraphs. No term, sunset, condition or report date. EO 10954 amended the last paragraph (attached). EO 10738, which EO 10906 supersedes in part, is itself in the EO 12553 number list, so there is no revival question. Lead recorded, not an express end: the Tax Reform Act of 1976 rewrote sec. 6103 of the Internal Revenue Code and may have displaced the inspection-by-order system before 1986; no statutory text is held, the OLRC note at 26 U.S.C. 6103 note (which lists this order and says EO 12553 revoked it) does not record any earlier statutory ending, and a statutory displacement is not an express end, so EO 12553 is the first express end and the date is an upper bound.

later_events.mechanism: partial amendment by EO 10954 (26 FR 6759, signed 1961-07-26; held official FR text): 'the last paragraph of Executive Order No. 10906 ... be, and it is hereby, amended to read as follows', restating the effective-date and EO 10738 supersession paragraph with the words 'the Internal Revenue Code of 1939 or' dropped from the estate and gift-tax returns reference. EO 10954 states 'This order shall be effective as of January 18, 1961', the day EO 10906 took effect on filing, so the amendment is effective 1961-01-18 (signed 1961-07-26). It changes the last paragraph only and the inspection authority in the first paragraph is untouched, so it is a partial amendment and not an end. EO 10954 has its own row in the EO 12553 table

uary 18,1961.

research_rationale: EO 10906 (signed 1961-01-17, 26 FR 508; Internal Revenue Code of 1954 secs. 6103(a) and 6106), read in full from the held FR text, has two paragraphs: an authority for inspection of returns by classes of persons and State and Federal establishments, and an effective-on-filing paragraph that supersedes EO 10738 in part. It has no own-terms end. EO 10954 (1961-07-26, effective as of 1961-01-18, held official text) restated the last paragraph; attached. EO 12553 (51 FR 7237, signed February 25, 1986; held official FR text, text sha256 6361bdc5...) says 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked' and lists the order in its 'No. Subject' table; it has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is READ as effective on signing, the on_signing reading 1986-02-25 (FR publication 1986-03-03 is not an effective date); this date is an upper bound, not a certified end. EO 10954 is also listed in EO 12553's table, so the amending order is ended by its own row. Earlier-end test: OFR catalog, U.S. Code and eCFR show only EO 10954, EO 10738 (superseded in part by this order, not the reverse) and EO 12553; no other held order names EO 10906. The Tax Reform Act of 1976 rewrite of IRC 6103 is an unheld statutory lead, recorded and not treated as an express end; the claim's end is therefore an upper bound on the on_signing reading.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12553 (EO 12553, 51 FR 7237, read once in full): one operative sentence revoking the listed orders 'and any amendments thereto', no savings, continuation, transfer, exception or delayed-effect wording, so EO 12553 saves and transfers nothing. Own-residual check, reading EO 10906 and EO 10954 in full: EO 10906 opens tax returns to inspection by classes of persons and State and Federal establishments under rules in a separate Treasury decision; it confers no property, funds, personal rights, delegation of functions or continuing duty of its own, and inspections made while it stood are completed acts. The one-time supersession of EO 10738 in part is a completed act and EO 10738 is itself revoked by EO 12553. The Treasury decision it refers to is a separate instrument whose status EO 12553 does not decide. S0 prefill (none_after_bounded_search) KEPT. Bounded search: EO 10906, EO 10954 and EO 12553 in full; U.S. Code and eCFR hits (machine) show only the revocation note.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Whole order (1961-08-23, effective on filing for publication, filed 1961-08-24; 26 FR 8001): returns made in respect of the listed taxes under the Internal Revenue Codes of 1939 and 1954 'shall be open to inspection by the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations' for its studies on coordinating tax laws and fiscal relations, under the Treasury decision approved the same day, and the order is effective upon its filing. The dossier clause covers the whole operative text (enacting words, the inspection authority and the effective-date sentence), so the inventory is complete. No term, sunset, condition or report date and no stated end of the Commission's studies. No held order amends, supersedes or revokes EO 10962 other than EO 12553 (number search of held fr-originals texts: only unrelated proclamation 10962 of 2025; OFR catalog edges: only EO 12553). Lead recorded, not an express end: the Tax Reform Act of 1976 rewrite of IRC 6103 and the Commission's later statutory history; no statutory text is held and the OLRC note records only the 1986 revocation, so EO 12553 is the first express end and the date is an upper bound.

By virtue of the authority vested in me  
by sections 55(a), as amended, 1204, and  
1604(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of  
1939 (53 Stat. 29, 171, 186; 54 Stat. 1008;  
55 Stat. 722; 26 U.S.C. (1952 Ed.) 55(a),  
1204, and 1604(c)), and by sections  
6103(a) and 6106 of the Internal Reve­
nue Code of 1954 (68 A Stat. 753, 756; 26  
U.S.C. 6103(a), 6106), it is hereby or­
dered that returns made in respect of  
taxes imposed by chapter 1, subchapters  
A, B, D, and E of chapter 2, subchapter B  
of chapter 3, chapters 4, 6, and 7, sub­
chapter C of chapter 9, chapters 12 and  
21, subchapter A of chapter 29, and chap­
ter 30 of the Internal Revenue Code of  
1939 and returns made in respect of taxes  
imposed by chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 12,  
23, and 32, subchapters B, C, and D of  
chapter 33, and subchapter B of chapter  
37 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954  
shall be open to inspection by the Ad­
visory Commission on Intergovernmental  
Relations for the purpose of making  
studies and investigations in connection  
with the performance of its function of  
recommending methods of coordinating  
and simplifying tax laws and adminis­
trative practices to achieve a more or­
derly and less competitive fiscal relation­
ship between the levels of government  
and to reduce the burden of compliance  
for taxpayers. Such inspection shall be  
in accordance and upon compliance with  
the rules prescribed by the Secretary of  
the Treasury in the Treasury "decision  
approved by me this date,1  relating to the 
inspection of such returns by the Ad­
visory Commission on Intergovernmental  
Relations.
This Executive order shall be effec­
tive upon its filing for publication in the  
F ederal R egister.

research_rationale: EO 10962 (signed 1961-08-23, 26 FR 8001; Internal Revenue Code of 1939 secs. 55(a), 1204 and 1604(c) and of 1954 secs. 6103(a) and 6106), read in full from the held FR text, is a single authorization for inspection of tax returns by the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations, effective upon filing. It has no own-terms end and no later amending order is held. EO 12553 (51 FR 7237, signed February 25, 1986; held official FR text, text sha256 6361bdc5...) says 'to eliminate Executive Orders that are no longer necessary, it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and any amendments thereto, are revoked' and lists the order in its 'No. Subject' table; it has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is READ as effective on signing, the on_signing reading 1986-02-25 (FR publication 1986-03-03 is not an effective date); this date is an upper bound, not a certified end. Earlier-end test: the machine OFR catalog, U.S. Code and eCFR searches (two hits each) are the 1986 revocation and the OLRC note listing it; the held-text number search finds no other order naming it. The Tax Reform Act of 1976 rewrite of IRC 6103 is an unheld statutory lead, recorded and not treated as an express end, so the end is an upper bound on the on_signing reading.

savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_12553 (EO 12553, 51 FR 7237, read once in full): one operative sentence revoking the listed orders 'and any amendments thereto', no savings, continuation, transfer, exception or delayed-effect wording, so EO 12553 saves and transfers nothing. Own-residual check, reading EO 10962 in full: it opens specified tax returns to inspection by the Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations under a separate Treasury decision; it confers no property, funds, personal rights, delegation or continuing duty, and inspections made while it stood are completed acts. By virtue of the authority vested in me 
by the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403) 
and section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, 
and as President of the United States, it 
is ordered that paragraph 3 (a) of Execu­
tive Order No. 9721 of May 10,1946, pro­
viding for the transfer of personnel to 
public international organizations in 
which the United States Government 
participates, be, and it is hereby, modi­
fied as follows:
The provision which requires that serv­
ice in the public international organiza­
tion to which the employee is transferred 
shall be terminated within three years 
from the date of such transfer to entitle 
the employee to the reemployment rights 
conferred by the said paragraph is modi­
fied so that Gerald C. Gross, a former em­
ployee of the Federal Communications 
Commission who is now employed by the 
International Telecommunication Union, 
and to whom the provisions of the said 
Executive Order No. 9721 became appli­
cable pursuant to paragraph 4 thereof, 
shall be entitled to such reemployment 
rights if his service with the said Inter­
national Telecommunication Union is 
terminated without prejudice within five 
years from the date of the beginning of 
his service with such Union; provided 
that he complies with all other provisions 
of the said Executive order with respect 
to such reemployment.
